metas.name: Alaska - Infrastructure - Alaskan Pipeline
metas.note: The Alaskan pipeline which is usually visible from main roads, can be seen at these points. This is an easy way to identify Alaska as there are no similar pipelines in the rest of the US.

metas.name: Alaska - Infrastructure - Anchorage Hydrant
metas.note: Fire hydrants in Anchorage are typically pale pink or pale yellow in colour.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Alaska - Infrastructure - Fairbanks Hydrant
metas.note: Fire hydrants in Fairbanks are commonly either bright yellow or a combination of colours (most commonly yellow and blue).
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Bridge
metas.note: The single-lane bridge, connecting the islands of Manu’a and Olosega, can be easily recognized by the thin wire guardrail, with the two islands on either side of the bridge.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Coconut / Powerline / Guardrail
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river.

The short stretch immediately east of the river only shows the Coconuts in the distance towards East. There's both a Powerline and a Guardrail.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Manu'a/Olosega Sand Road
metas.note:
From slightly North of the town entry of Olosega until the southernmost house WEST of the road, you will have a plain sand road, with no grass verge in the middle.

This is the only road of this kind on the two islands with this Google Car.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Ofu Airport
metas.note: Ofu Airport is small with a concrete runway. The Google Car covering it has two orange straps on the roof. Many palm trees can also be seen on the other side of the runway.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Super Straight Road
metas.note: This section of the Rte 014 is by far the straightest covered road on Tutuila. Use the road angle to confirm. The appearance is quite varied, but it's also very flat

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Asphalt
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West and have Asphalt pavement, you're on the far west part of the road.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Coconut / No Powerline
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river.

The short stretch immediately east of the little sideroad has no powerline, unlike the other locs with Coconuts.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Coconut / Powerline / No Guardrail
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river.

On this stretch, if you have a powerline, but no guardrail, you're east of the river, and west of the small sideroad on the map.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Concrete / Overgrown / Guardrail / No Powerline
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road.

If additionally, you have a guardrail, but no powerline, you're on the east-west stretch west of the river.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Concrete / Overgrown / No Guardrail
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road.

If additionally, you have no guardrail, you're on the stretch marked on the second image, south of a smooth coast protrusion west of the river.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Overgrown - Powerline
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road.

If additionally, you have a powerline visible, you're on the SW-NE stretch immediately west of the river.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Visible Coast / Guardrail
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you have the coast North of you, with no significant vegetation in the way, you're on the Easternmost part of the road, east of the little sideroad.

The western half of this stretch has a guardrail, the eastern half does not.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Visible Coast / No Guardrail
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you have the coast North of you, with no significant vegetation in the way, you're on the Easternmost part of the road, east of the little sideroad.

The western half of this stretch has a guardrail, the eastern half does not.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tutuila Airport
metas.note: On the roads along the airport on Tutuila, you will always see these fences surrounding the airport. This is obviously common for airports, but since Tutuila only has one airstrip, this road is a free 5k together with the Tutuila car.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tutuila Concrete Road
metas.note: If you are on Tutuila and have a Concrete Road with no coast visible, you're on the far Eastern Part of the island, between Onenoa and Matatula Elementary school.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Bariloche Taxi
metas.note: This taxi with the white body, blue roof and blue logo is unique to the city of Bariloche.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Buenos Aires Taxi
metas.note: This taxi with a black body and yellow roof is common in Buenos Aires. Note that taxis from Jujuy and Rosarío have the same combination. However, Buenos Aires is the only city where the taxi has the middle bar (behind the driver) painted.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Comodoro Rivadavia Taxi
metas.note: This all white taxi with a black logo is unique to Comodoro Rivadavia.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Cordoba km-marker
metas.note: You can find these unique markers on provincial roads in Cordoba.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Cordoba Taxi
metas.note: These all green or all yellow taxis with an oval shape beneath the driver door are unique to Cordoba.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Jujuy Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in Jujuy have a black body and a yellow roof. Notably, only the top of the roof is yellow, making it distinct from Rosario or Buenos Aires taxis.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - km-marker
metas.note: Argentinian kilometer markers are typically white with a black strip displaying the road number at the top. RN stands for ruta national (white on the map), RP stands for ruta provincial (green on the map).

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - La Pampa Junction Sign
metas.note: T-Junctions in La Pampa sometimes have these yellow rectangular signs, with a chevron pattern on the bottom, and the Road Number(s) above, with an arrow on both sides.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - La Plata Taxi
metas.note: La Plata has white taxis with green elements.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Latvian-style Poles
metas.note: Within Argentina, these Latvian style wooden hook poles are unique to La Rioja and Mendoza.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Mendoza Taxi
metas.note: This black and yellow taxi is unique to Mendoza. Jujuy, Rosario and Buenos Aires also have black and yellow taxis, but on those taxis, the body is completely black.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Neuquen Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in Neuquen are all yellow. What distinguishes them from Cordoba taxis is that their doors have no logos or paintings on them.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Resistencia Taxi
metas.note: Taxis with a red-white-green stripe (hungarian flag) are unique to Resistencia.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Rosario Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in Rosario have a black body and a yellow roof. The outer bars are yellow, while the middle bar (behind the driver) is black. This makes them distinguishable from taxis in Jujuy and Buenos Aires.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Salta Taxi
metas.note: Red taxis with a black stripe are unique to Salta.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - San Juan Taxi
metas.note: White taxis with a yellow roof are unique to San Juan.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - San Luis Taxi
metas.note: White taxis with two light-blue stripes (resembling the Argentinian flag) are unique to San Luis.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Santiago del Estero Taxi
metas.note: White taxis with light-green roofs are unique to Santiago del Estero.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Single Hook Insulator
metas.note: In Mendoza, poles with a single insulator attached to the side of the pole can be found.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Tucuman Pole ID
metas.note: White vertical pole stickers with several digits can be found in Tucumán.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Tucuman Taxi
metas.note: These old-school, white taxis with a yellow-black checkerboard stripe are unique to Tucuman.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - ∀-Poletop - Round
metas.note: The ∀-Poletop is found in South Australia and New South Wales. In SA, the pole will be a stobie pole, while in NSW it will be round.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - 130 km/h speed limit
metas.note: Within Australia, a speed limit of 130 km/h can only be found in the Northern Territory.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - 25 school zone
metas.note: South Australia is the only Australian state that uses a 25 speed limit in school zones.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - 90° poletop
metas.note: Poletops in Tasmania often consist of a thin metal crossbar bent 90 degrees to form an L-shape.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - ACT Bus Stop
metas.note: Unique to Australian Capital Territory (Canberra).

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Black pole marking
metas.note:
These black markings are specific to electricity poles in Queensland. They are often accompanied by diagonal numbers.

They are almost exclusively found between Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - black-white striped bollard
metas.note: These black-and-white stripy bollards are unique to Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - black-yellow striped bollard
metas.note: This black-and-yellow bollard is exclusive to Queensland.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Blue Square on Pole
metas.note: Melbourne poles commonly feature these white, rectangular stickers, with a smaller blue square inside it.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - bollard with brown bottom
metas.note: Bollards with brown paint at the bottom are most commonly found in Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - bollard with short reflector
metas.note: Reflectors that are shorter than the regular ones are most common in Queensland and South Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Brisbane Streetsign
metas.note: Identified by the little symbol.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - C-Road
metas.note: Roads that start with the letter ‘C’ are only found in Victoria and Tasmania. In addition, South Australia has some C roads near the border with Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Charters Towers Red Roads
metas.note: As a general rule in Queensland state, Australia, red tinted roads are found mostly around Charters Towers (especially when you have more trees), they can also be found on the A2 near label, and the 1 further north. These areas are indicated in the distribution, but there may be minor exceptions.
metas.footer: Source: Meat of the Day on ScripterCord

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - concrete pole
metas.note: According to a 2006 review, 64% of all concrete poles are located in the state of Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Darwin Bus Stop
metas.note: The city of Darwin, NT uses concrete shelters as bus stops.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Dorat Road
metas.note: Dorat Road (23) in the Northern Territory can be easily recognized thanks to its distinct Darwin area landscape and lack of road lines.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Dotted Concrete Pole
metas.note: These round concrete poles with dots going up on them are found in New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - flat signpost
metas.note: Some signposts in South Australia and Western Australia are flat rather than round.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - fluoresecent sign border
metas.note: Road signs with a fluorescent border are almost exclusively found in Queensland.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Gold Coast Streetsign
metas.note: This street sign is unique to Gold Coast City Council.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Green Dot on Pole
metas.note: This Green Dot on poles is sometimes found in New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - green pole bottom
metas.note: Poles in Western Australia often have green painted bases, and sometimes a white sticker or a red and white band attached.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - green property marker
metas.note: You can find these dark green property markers on the sides of roads in Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Hanging Insulator
metas.note: These poles with hanging insulators are found in Queensland and New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - hydrant with blue circle
metas.note: You can find these white hydrant poles that feature a blue circle and a red section on top of it in Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - hydrant with red top
metas.note: These fire hydrants with red painted tops are unique to Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - License Plate - Slim NSW
metas.note: Very slim license plate (similar to Swiss front plates) are found in Victoria and New South Wales. While in Victoria, you can usually see two blue blocks of texts, in NSW they appear plain.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - License Plate - Slim Victoria
metas.note: Very slim license plate (similar to Swiss front plates) are found in Victoria and New South Wales. While in Victoria, you can usually see two blue blocks of texts, in NSW they appear plain.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - License Plate - Taxi - Blue
metas.note: Blue plates on Taxis are found exclusively in New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Mount Kosciuszko
metas.note:
All-yellow road lines can be seen on roads around Mount Kosciuszko.

In addition, a unique white truck with a snorkel, and cab guard can be found.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - No-Stopping-sign with text
metas.note: The white ‘No Stopping’ and ‘No Parking’ signs that include text are unique to the Australian Capital Territory.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - NSW Bus Stop
metas.note: New South Wales uses these two designs for bus stops. One is blue and has a white B in a circle with it, the other has the signpost bending over the actual sign.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - NSW guardrail ending
metas.note: This guardrail ending, featuring a black dash on a yellow background, is almost exclusive to New South Wales and the ACT.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - NT License Plate
metas.note: License Plates in Northern Territory have bright red lettering which shines through the blur. Looks kind of similar to the Queensland plates, which are a bit darker.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Octagonal Pole
metas.note: Octagonal Poles in Australia are found mostly in and around Sydney.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - olive-green possum guard
metas.note: Olive-green possum guards are only found on electricity poles in Tasmania.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - H
metas.note: The 'H' poletag is found in New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - HP
metas.note: This poletag with 'HP' is found in New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - NSW - Horizontal
metas.note: Within New South Wales, purely horizontal poletags (i.e. no vertical on the same pole), are not found around Sydney.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - NSW - Letter Code
metas.note: In NSW, poletags in the triangle formed by Sydney, Newcastle and Scone (view map) almost always have one or two letters in their codes.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - NSW - Vertical / Outer White
metas.note: Within NSW, these vertical plates with white ends are not found near Sydney. Note that otherwise, vertical plates will be close to Sydney within NSW.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - QLD - Vertical
metas.note: Poletags with a blue sticker, and a vertical steel tag are found in Queensland, north of Rockhampton.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - Vertical / Regular
metas.note:
Within NSW, regular vertical poletags are found south and west of Sydney.

Note that if the poletags have white ends on each side, they are NOT close to Sydney, but rather throughout the rest of NSW.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - Yellow T
metas.note: This poletag which consists of rectangular yellow stickers that usually form a T, is exclusive to New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Queensland Bus Stop
metas.note: Bus stops in Queensland have a yellow signpost bending over the actual sign.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Queensland License Plate
metas.note: The Queensland License Plate has dark red letters which can shine through the blur. Looks similar to the NT plate, which has a lighter red tone. There is also an old, green version, which could theoretically show up.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Queensland poletop
metas.note: Queensland features these unique pole tops with coils that are angled upwards on the sides.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Queensland sticker
metas.note: Circular blue stickers can be found on Queensland poles. You may occasionally see the same type of sticker in a different colour, or with the colour almost completely faded.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - red "No Stopping" sign
metas.note: New South Wales is the only state to use red ‘No Stopping’ signs.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Roadline Gap with no Reflector
metas.note: In South Australia and the ACT, you can sometimes find gaps in the outer roadlines. If this gap has no reflector, it is South Australia.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt - Archived This meta was removed from the PlonkIt guide. The link leads you to the archived page.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Roadline gap with Reflector
metas.note: In South Australia and the ACT, you can sometimes find gaps in the outer roadlines. In ACT, there will always be a reflector in the gap. This can also appear occasionally in South Australia.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt - Archived This meta was removed from the PlonkIt guide. The link leads you to the archived page.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - rusty holey pole
metas.note: These rusty metal poles, containing several holes, are unique to the Northern Territory, and rarely the northern part of Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Sloped Kerbs
metas.note: You can sometimes see sloped kerbs in Perth, where it gradually declines to the road, whilst in other cities kerbs go straight down at a 90 degree angle.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - South Australia Bus Stop
metas.note: Orange signpost, sign extending over the signpost.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Stobie pole
metas.note: The iconic Stobie pole, made of steel and concrete, is specific to South Australia. Outside of SA, it sometimes occurs in Broken Hill, NSW or Tasmania.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Sydney Streetsign
metas.note: This street sign is unique to the City of Sydney.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Tasmania Bus Stop
metas.note: Different versions, but usually have "Metro" written on them.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - thin "Keep Left" sign
metas.note: Some ‘Keep Left’ signs in New South Wales, Queensland, and the Northern Territory use this thinner version, which does not include an arrow.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - traffic light with no outline
metas.note: Traffic lights without a border are found in Northern Territory, South Australia and Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - traffic light with white outline
metas.note: Traffic lights with a white outline around the frame are found in the eastern and western states of WA, QLD, NSW, ACT and Tas. Traffic lights without a border are found in the remaining, central states.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Triple Broken Roadlines
metas.note: The Sturt Highway from Wentworth to Wagga Wagga can have triple broken centre lines. They can also be found on other major roads in NSW, such as the Gwydir Highway.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - upward pointing trident pole
metas.note: A trident-like pole top with the insulators pointing to the top can sometimes be seen in Western Australia and Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Victoria Bus Stop
metas.note: Bus Stops in Victoria can be recognized by their color scheme: White-Orange-Black-Grey-White.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Victoria License Plate
metas.note: License plates in Victoria have a little small triangle at the top, which can sometimes be recognized through the blur.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Victoria poletop
metas.note: Victorian pole tops feature 3 circular coils; 2 on the sides, and 1 vertical one at the top. At times, other extensions can be seen on these poles.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Western Australia Bus Stop
metas.note: Bus Stops in Australia are marked by these horizontal poles with information on them.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Western Australia License Plate
metas.note: Western Australian License Plate have blue letters and a thin blue stripe at the top, which can sometimes be recognized through the blur.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - white directional sign
metas.note: White directional signs can only be found in Tasmania.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - white property marker
metas.note: You can find these white property markers on the sides of roads in South Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Yellow License Plate
metas.note: Yellow license plates can occasionally be found in New South Wales. Most license plates are still white, though. The old design of Western Australian plates is also yellow, so you might stumble upon them in WA very rarely.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - yellow signpost
metas.note: Yellow signposts are specific to Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - ш-shaped poletop
metas.note: Poletops that resemble the cyrillic letter ш are unique to South Australia.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - 2 Ridge Insulator
metas.note: Memorize the distribution map.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - 3 Ridge Insulator
metas.note:
Most commonly found in Paraiba in the North, and in Parana, Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro. It's pretty rare.

Memorize the distribution map for more details.

Note by MB: They're also different to the lollipop insulator, where the ridges have different sizes.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - 4 Ridge Insulator
metas.note:
Widespread, but can still resolve some 50/50s. Memorize the map.

Also, in Sao Paulo, it's common in Sao Paulo city, and uncommon outside of it.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - 5 Ridges Insulator
metas.note: Insulators with 5 ridges are very common in Sao Paulo.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - 90° Crossbar
metas.note: Right angle top bars are common in Brasília
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Aerodynamic Lamp
metas.note: Aerodynamic Lamp Heads are common in Fortaleza.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Alagoas Lamp
metas.note: Different colors possible
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Aracaju Lamp Arm ID
metas.note: Unique ID on a common lamp head. Sometimes, you can't see much of the code, only zip ties.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Aracaju Road Sign
metas.note: Aracaju, Sergipe
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Barra Do Garcas Lamp Arm
metas.note: Barra Do Garcas, Mato Grosso (border to Goias)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Belem ID
metas.note: Lots of rare pole IDs in the city
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Belo Horizonte Lamp
metas.note: Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Bend Attached to Pole
metas.note: The vast majority of poles in Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Pará, Amapá, Rio Grande do Norte, Pernambuco and Santa Catarina have the lamp arm attached to the pole, as opposed to it being attached with a plate, which is much more common generally.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Big Electricity Counter on Pole
metas.note:
Big electricity counters on the pole are most common in Mato Grosso, Para and Amapa.

Unlike their smaller version, they do not appear in Paraiba.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Black&Yellow Bollards
metas.note: Black & Yellow bollards of different kinds are common in Salvador.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Blue ID
metas.note: Unique to Rio Branco
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Blue Lamp Arm ID
metas.note: Small, blue, hanging from the lamp arm. Found in Cuiaba (bend attached to pole), and in the cities of Riberao Preto and Sao Paulo (normal lamp arm)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Boa Vista ID
metas.note: Boa Vista, Roraima
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - BR-101 in the Northeast
metas.note:
This road is divided. What makes it special is that one direction as asphalt and the other direction has concrete pavement.

This does not apply to the entire road anymore
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Brasilia Streetsign
metas.note: Brasilia, Distrito Federal
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Brown Mushroom Insulator
metas.note: Pernambuco sometimes uses these brown mushroom insulators.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Campinas Sidewalk
metas.note: The city of Campinas, SP is known for it's unique and artistic patterns of black and white stones on its sidewalks.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Cascavel Black Number Arrow
metas.note: A tiny black pole paint, containing a white number with a triangle-shaped arrow. Unique to Cascavel, Parana.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Cascavel Blue Lamp
metas.note: The town of Cascavel, Paraná uses this blue lamp. However, in newer coverage it is very rare to find.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Ceara Lamp Arms
metas.note: Lamps in Ceará often have a fancy and colourful arm, whether as lampposts or attached to utility poles. It sometimes says the town on the arm.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Ceara Poletop
metas.note: This assymetrical pole with no supports appears statewide in Ceara and sometimes Rondonia. (The Sao Paulo pole has a support bar)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Center White Lines
metas.note: White Center lines are very common in Joao Pessoa. Yellow dashed lines are rare.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Chessboard Sidewalk
metas.note: The sidewalks with a chessboard pattern are common in Curitiba, PR.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Cobblestone Pavement
metas.note: Cobblestone pavement is most common in the northeast and in Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Colorful Signpost
metas.note: These colorful, thick signposts can be found in different cities in the state of Sao Paulo.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Compact Electricity Counter on Pole
metas.note:
An electricity counter with a compact design can be seen in Mato Grosso, Para, Amapa and Paraiba.

The "less compact" variant with several counters does not exist in Paraiba.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Concrete Trash Bins
metas.note: Brazil often uses metal trash baskets outside houses. In Acre and Rondônia, however, it is much more common to see them made of concrete.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Connector in Bend
metas.note: Meta for Sao Paulo. Only counts when the connector is pointing downwards. The connectors pointing upwards are generic.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Corroded Streetsign
metas.note: All the street signs in Palmas are corroded.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Crossbar with no support
metas.note: Crossbars with no support bars are almost exclusively found in Piaui, Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte and Alagoas. They also frequently appear in the North-East in general, and in Rondonia and Roraima.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Curitiba Sidewalk
metas.note: The two most typical sidewalk patterns in Curitiba, PR.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Dark Brown Insulator on Grey Base
metas.note: These dark brown insulators with grey bases are found almost exclusively in Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Divided Highway
metas.note: São Paulo has far more divided highways than any other state.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Embedded Pole ID
metas.note: Yellow plate embedded into pole. Mainly in Maranhao, spill into Para and Piaui.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Exremely Long Insulator
metas.note:
This one is basically a sub-category of the 6+ Ridge Insulator. It's common in Para, Parana, Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul.

However, it's not always easy to tell apart, but the longer the insulator feels, the more you should consider those states.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Campo Mourão
metas.note: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Campo Mourão.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Cidade Gaucha
metas.note: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Cidade Gaucha. Notably, it's very similar to the one from Campo Mourao.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Goioere
metas.note: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one - with the yellow support - is unique to the town of Goioere. However, in newer coverage, the yellow supports are rarer to find.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Loanda
metas.note: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one - with a plain white lamp and no painted patterns on it - is unique to the town of Loanda.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Umuarama
metas.note: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Umuarama. It is strikingly similar to the lamp from Cidade Gaucha.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Umuarama
metas.note: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific, uniquely shaped one is unique to the town of Umuarama.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Florianopolis Pole
metas.note: Poles on Florianopolis, especially on Santa Catarina Island are painted white with blue and red stripes.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Florianopolis Sign
metas.note: Sometimes also with a white line instead of a red line.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fortaleza ID
metas.note: These two types of IDs are common in Fortaleza (two pictures)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Gamma + Box
metas.note:
Gamma pole with an electricity box at the end of the crossbeam. Most common in Belem, Salvador and Rio de Janeiro. Can appear occasionally in Ceara and Alagoas.

In RJ, they are particularly common in Sao Goncalo, but appear statewide.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Goias Pole ID
metas.note: The Goias pole ID uses yellow paint with black numbers or a black plate with yellow numbers. Unlike the Bahia and Pernambuco IDs, the ID consists exclusively of digits.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Grass Verge
metas.note: Grass verges between the sidewalk and the road are common in Curitiba.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Green Lamp
metas.note: There are three large cities with green lamps: Cuiaba, Manaus and Vitoria
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Hexagonal Pavement
metas.note: Roads with hexagonal concrete tiles can be found across Brazil, but they are more common in Santa Catarina and Minas Gerais.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - High attached ID
metas.note: Yellow plate attached by zip tie or metal strip. If it is higher up on the pole, it's in Pernambuco.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Holey Ladder Pole
metas.note: Ladder Poles with holes in them are very common in Joao Pessoa (but not unique)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Horizontal Insulators
metas.note: Poles with horizontal insulators are very common in Pará and less so in Mato Grosso. They are rarely found in Acre, Amapá, Tocantins, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Horizontal Insulators with Top
metas.note: Poles that have one insulator on top and alternating horizontal insulators can be found in Mato Grosso and southern Acre. It is also very rare in Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Huge Electric Box on Pole
metas.note: Electric meter boxes can be seen in other cities, but in Cuiaba, there are usually 3-6 or even more on one pole.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Huge pole ID
metas.note: This rather large pole ID is common in Betim, Minas Gerais.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Imperatriz holey ID
metas.note: This city ID is distinct thanks to the holes on the sides.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Imperatriz Ornate Lamp
metas.note: Imperatriz, Maranhao
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Internet Poster
metas.note: Internet Advertisements attached to poles are very common in Natal. Mnemonic: Internatal :)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Ipiranga Lamp
metas.note: These red lamps that resemble Belém lamps can be found in the neighborhood of Ipiranga in Florianopolis.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Irregular Cobblestone
metas.note: Cobblestone roads with randomly sized stones are most common in southeast Rio Grande do Sul and Minas Gerais.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Itumbiara Red Lamp
metas.note: Itumbiara, Goias
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Joao de Barro nests
metas.note: These spheres on top of utility poles are João-de-Barro nests. They are common across the south of Brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Joao Pessoa Stone Pavement
metas.note: Distinct stone sidewalks & driveways in Joao Pessoa.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Joinville Lamp
metas.note: Joinville, Santa Catarina
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Joinville Street Sign
metas.note: Not to be confused with the Curitiba sign, which can also be attached to a pole.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Kilometer Marker with Phone Number
metas.note: Phone numbers can sometimes be seen underneath kilometre markers in São Paulo.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Lack of Poles
metas.note: Suspicious lack of poles, and curved lamp posts in their place, are indicative of Brasília.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Little Guy Lamp
metas.note: This cute lamp is unique to Gurupi.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Lollipop Insulators
metas.note: These insulators are spherical or cone shaped and suspended on a rod above the insulator bar. They are often referred to as “lollipop” insulators. They are very common in Rio Grande de Norte, Paraíba, Pernambuco, and more rarely, Sergipe.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Londrina Black Pole ID
metas.note: These black pole IDs are common in the state of Paraná, except for the capital Curitiba. If the black pole has a decimal marker (.) in the number, it's in Londrina.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Londrina Blue Number on Pole
metas.note: The town of Londrina, Paraná sometimes has little blue numbers painted on its poles.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Low Attached ID
metas.note: Yellow plate attached by zip tie or metal strip. If it is lower on the pole, it is RGDN.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - MA006
metas.note: Most of this road has a thick (1m) stripe of red dirt on the sides of the road. The road is oriented North-South and frequently shows Babassu palms
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Macapa Lamp
metas.note: Macapa, Amapa
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Macapa Pole ID
metas.note: Macapa, Amapa
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Maceio ID
metas.note: These two IDs are rare but unique to Maceio.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Maceio Lamp
metas.note: Long posts with top arm bend and yellow or grey top dot at the bottom.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Maceio Streetsign
metas.note: Also available in blue.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Manaus Pole ID
metas.note: Pole IDs in Manaus are usually above the lamp attachment.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Maraba Skull Box
metas.note: Yellow skull stickers are common on electric boxes in Maraba.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - MGDS Flag
metas.note: In urban settings, state flags might show up. Might pay off sometimes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Minas Gerais ID with 0/1
metas.note: These pole IDs are specific for Minas Gerais. If they start with 0 or 1, it's Belo Horizonte.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Natal ID
metas.note: Natal, Rio Grande do Norte
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Neon-Yellow Horizontal ID
metas.note: Neon-yellow horizontal IDs are specific to Sao Paulo. Do not confuse with Campo Grande or Vitoria (they have vertical, and smaller, neon-yellow IDs)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Neon-Yellow Pole ID
metas.note: Neon-yellow, vertical IDs can be found in Campo Grande, MS and Vitoria, ES. Do not confuse with horizontal neon-yellow IDs (Sao Paulo)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Onitel Sticker
metas.note: Unique to Luziania, GO
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Open Electric Box
metas.note: Open or trashed electric boxes appear frequently in Maraba and Santarém (both Para).
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Orange Lamp
metas.note: Orange Lamps are common in Belem.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Orange Lamp Arm
metas.note: Very common in Teresina, one of the most well-known urban Brazil metas.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Outer Dashed Lines
metas.note: Outer Dashed Lines can rarely be found in Rio Grande do Norte or other northeast states.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Para specific Pole ID
metas.note: Pare uses these state-wide pole IDs.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Paraiba ID
metas.note: This ID is uncommon, but unique to Paraiba (most common in the capital Joao Pessoa).
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Paraiba Lamp
metas.note: The shape matters.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Parana Black Paint Pole ID
metas.note: Pole IDs in Paraná are usually made up of black paint and yellow or white painted text. They do not appear in the capital of Paraná: Curitiba.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess, Plonk It

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Parana Black Square
metas.note: This tiny black paint is rarely found on larger poles in Paraná. Still worth a quick scan, especially in urban locs.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Parana Road Pole Paint
metas.note: Utility poles in Paraná on intersections are sometimes painted with the street name. This is because metal signs are expensive. This is also possible on Northern Rio Grande do Sul ladder poles. An exception is the town of Sinop, Mato Grosso.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess, PlonkIt

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - PARE on stone
metas.note: Stone road markings are unique to Caxias do Sul, RS.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pencil Pole Top
metas.note: This little hat on the top, which makes the whole pole resemble a pencil, is most common in Rio de Janeiro, but can also be found in Manaus and Distrito Federal.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Piles of Dirt Meta
metas.note: Common in Boa Vista
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole Company
metas.note: Electricity company names in Brazil are commonly engraved onto the poles, with their names sometimes corresponding to state names. For example, CELPA stands for Para, COSERN for Rio Grande do Norte or COELCE for Ceara.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole Paint starting with letter
metas.note: Yellow paint with black numbers, starts with a letter. Possible in Bahia and Pernambuco. The letter is often specific to a town. Goias uses similar paint IDs, but they consist only of digits.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole-Attached Sign
metas.note: Some poles in Curitiba, PR have street signs attached to them. Curitiba still uses regular, generic street signs, though.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole-Wrapped Sign
metas.note: These blue pole-wrapped signs are unique to Campo Grande.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Porto Alegre ID
metas.note: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Porto Velho Pole ID
metas.note: Porto Velho, Rondonia
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Recife Lamp
metas.note: Recife, Pernambuco
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rectangle on Pole Arm
metas.note: Unique for Recife. Can be faded or even have different colors. It's the shape that matters.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Red Brick Pavement
metas.note: Some roads in Acre are made of red brick.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Red Gravel
metas.note: Most roads in Piauí have red gravel on the side of the road. Some roads in Generation 4 now have tarmac and kerbs, but some gravel shoulders remain.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Red Sticker on Lamp
metas.note: This red sticker below the lamp is unique to Fortaleza.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio de Janeiro Lamp
metas.note: Curvy lamp arm, usually big head.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio de Janeiro Landbridge
metas.note: This map west of the city of Rio de Janeiro is unique due to the water in the south, the roadlines (double yellow - double broken yellow - single broken white) and the little wall in the North. Rio mountains can be seen in most sections of the road to the North.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio De Janeiro Polepaint
metas.note: This yellow polepaint, similar to Sao Paulo, but with all numbers, can be found in Rio de Janeiro.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio de Janeiro Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in Rio de Janeiro are completely yellow.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio Weird Pole
metas.note: When there is something out of the ordinary happening with the pole, it's Rio de Janeiro.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Roraima Lamps
metas.note: Lamps in Roraima have a similar style but have different colours in the main cities. Boa Vista, Normandia, and Mucajaí have red lamps, Rorainópolis has blue lamps, Pacaraima and Iracema have green, and Caracaraí has yellow.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Round Pole
metas.note: Alongside ladder poles, round poles can often be found across the south of Brazil, especially São Paulo. These poles are cylindrical and made of concrete.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Salvador Lamp Arm ID
metas.note: Long yellow ID on the lamp arm, can be very hard to spot.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Salvador Sidewalk
metas.note: Unique sidewalk, can have other black and white broken tile patterns.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Santarem Lamp
metas.note: Santarem, Para
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Luis ID
metas.note: This rare ID is specific to Sao Luis. However, the embedded Maranhao IDs are more common.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Luis Pointy Lamp
metas.note: Pointy front of lamp head, blue or yellow top light.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Paulo Lamp
metas.note: Straight long lamp neck, with tight top bend, usually thin head.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Paulo Pole
metas.note:
Assymetrical crossbeam and insulator position with a long support bar reaching to the middle of the longer part of the crossbeam.

Extremely common in Sao Paulo, common in Rio Grande do Sul. Less common Rio de Janeiro, Espirito Santo and Mato Grosso do Sul (where it appears most oftenly in Tres Lagoas). Rare in Mato Grosso.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Paulo Polepaint
metas.note: Sao Paulo Metropolitan Area has these yellow pole paints with a three letter code. The letters stand for the town. SPU is the most important code, standing for the main city.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Serra dos Orgaos
metas.note: This road can be found North of Rio de Janeiro (city). It is a concrete road with black tar behind the road lines.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Short Gamma + Box
metas.note: Short crossbeam, support bar and electricity box at the end of the crossbeam. Only found in Belem. (unlike the regular Gamma pole with box which can also be found in Salvador and Rio de Janeiro).
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Small Red Tactile Pavement
metas.note: Small tile, circular bumps, red tactile pavement is very common in Vitoria, ES. (Do not confuse with Florianopolis, which has large tile red tactile pavement).
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Southern Sidewalk
metas.note: You can often see pavements in Rio Grande do Sul that have brown tiles but are either jagged and random, or square. This style can sometimes be seen in Santa Catarina.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Speedbumps
metas.note: Yellow dashed lines and speedbumps are very common in Brasília. (but not unique)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Spool Insulators
metas.note: These insulators have a shape resembling a spool of thread. They are found mostly in Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo, and have been seen in Ceará.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Square Paint ID
metas.note: This ID with two sections, the upper one being a square with a number in it, appears in Pernambuco.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Striped Curbs
metas.note: Black and white striped curbs are common in Boa Vista.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Surprising Wooden Pole
metas.note: In Porto Alegre, there is noticeably more foliage, cleaner, and more spacious than any other city which makes the common wooden poles look somewhat out of place.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Teresina ID
metas.note: Long & Horizontal ID
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Thick Bottom Insulator
metas.note:
They're found almost anywhere, but can still resolve some 50/50s:

They are only rarely found in Rio Grande do Norte.

Also they're less common in Pernambuco, Parana, Santa Catarina.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Thin Long Insulator
metas.note: Insulators in Ceará can sometimes be uniquely long and thin. They are in Goiás too, but are rare.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Thin Red Stripe
metas.note: A road with a thin, red stripe out of gravel can be found east of Teresina, Piaui.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Araruna
metas.note: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Araruna.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Cianorte
metas.note: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Cianorte.

metas.note: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Loanda.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Maringa
metas.note: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Maringa.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Paranavai
metas.note: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Paranavai.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tocantins specific lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a short arm and top light is specific to Tocantins.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tocantins specific lamp
metas.note: This blue lamp with top light and the unique pattern on the underside is specific to Tocantins.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tocantins specific lamp
metas.note: This long blue lamp with a top light and a unique pattern on the underside is specific to Tocantins.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Transparent Mushroom Insulator
metas.note: Transparent, mushroom-shaped insulators are common in Alagoas. They less frequently appear in Coastal Santa Catarina. Rarely, they also appear in coastal Rio Grande do Sul, coastal Sao Paulo and in Sergipe.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Trident Pole
metas.note: Poles with these wide insulators in a trident formation are common in Maranhão. The insulator itself is common across many states, but not in this configuration.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Two Part Lamp - Goias Variant
metas.note:
2-part lamp, most commonly seen in Minas Gerais and Goias. This particular variant with a the pole visible underneath is more common in Goias.

Otherwise, this pole appears in Rio Grande do Norte and Rio Grande do Sul (very useful if you have North/South vibe), spill in Distrito Federal and extremely rarely in Para, Mato Grosso and Rondonia.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Two Part Lamp - Minas Gerais Variant
metas.note:
2-part lamp, most commonly seen in Minas Gerais and Goias. This particular variant - with both parts enveloping the lamp - is more common in Minas Gerais.

Otherwise, this pole appears in Rio Grande do Norte and Rio Grande do Sul (very useful if you have North/South vibe), spill in Distrito Federal and extremely rarely in Para, Mato Grosso and Rondonia.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Uberaba ID
metas.note: In Uberaba, pole IDs start with 2 or 3, and sometimes with 1. In Belo Horizonte, meanwhile, they start with 0 or 1. They do not appear in any other cities in MG.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Uneven Stone Pavement
metas.note: These uneven but mostly square stone roads are seen in western Rio Grande do Sul and west Santa Catarina. The soil will often be very dark in these regions too.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Vitoria Electric Boxes
metas.note: Metal electricity box, sandwiched between plastic electricity boxes are very common in Vitoria, ES.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Vitoria ID
metas.note: Red pole ID.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Vitoria Streetsign
metas.note: Unique streetsign design in Vitoria.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Weird Road Layout
metas.note: Roundabouts and weird layout roads that are mostly empty, and perfectly flat, are common in Palmas.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - White Mushroom Insulator
metas.note: Bahia uses these unique white insulators sometimes.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - WiFi-Password Pole-ID
metas.note: If you find pole IDs with codes that resemble WiFi-passwords (mix of digits, upper- and lowercase letters), you're in Curitiba, PR.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Wooden Pole
metas.note: Some states also use wooden poles. They are most commonly seen in Rio Grande do Sul, Roraima, Amazonas, and Rio de Janeiro.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Yellow Outer Lines
metas.note: Yellow outer lines on urban roads are very common in Curitiba.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Yellow Stick
metas.note: This yellow stick is common in Rio Branco, and often has a sign attached to it.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Zig-Zag lamp arm
metas.note: In Brazil, this Zig-Zag lamp arm is unique to Caxias do Sul.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - ZigZag-Topbar
metas.note: This pole configuration, featuring a zigzag-shaped top bar resting atop a flat crossbar, is exclusive to Ceara and Roraima. The pole is usually much larger than a regular electricity pole.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure -6+ Ridge Insulators
metas.note:
These insulators have six or more ridges.

Commonly found in:

  • Bahia, Tocantins, Maranhao
  • Para, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul
  • Parana Santa Catarina

Uncommon in:

  • Acre, Rondonia, Amapa
  • Piaui, Goias, Sao Paulo, RGDS

Rarely in:

  • RGDN, Rio de Janeiro

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Clay Brick Walls
metas.note: San Pedro de Atacama can be recognized by its clay brick walls, commonly with triangles at the top.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Concepcion Lamps
metas.note: Blue rectangular lamps with a yellow stripe can be found in Concepción.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Green Dome Lamps
metas.note: Lamps that look like green domes can be seen in Copiapo.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Letter Roads
metas.note: Chile uses a memorable regional road naming system, where the first letter increases between A and Y from north to south.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Orange Lamps
metas.note:
Orange lamps can most often be seen in Calama and Chañaral, and rarely in Antofagasta.

NOTE: Orange lamps can rarely be found in other smaller cities. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Orange Street Signs
metas.note: Orange street signs can be seen in the city of Lanco, present at almost every intersection.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Photocell Lamps
metas.note: Lamps in Santiago very commonly have photocells. You will rarely find them in other cities such as Valparaiso, Osorno and Loncoche.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Round Pole & Black Paint
metas.note: Round poles with black paint can be seen in the town of El Salvador.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Ruta 9
metas.note: All yellow lines on a concrete road are a good indicator that you are on the paved section of Ruta 9, in the very south of Chile. The landscape tends to be barren, grassy, and treeless.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Silver/Grey Lamp
metas.note: This lamp, with a silver top and grey bottom, can be found in Puerto Montt and Temuco.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Talca Lamps
metas.note: Grey lamps with a thin, flat top and a rounded underside can be found in Talca.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - White Pole Paint in the Desert
metas.note: Poles in Arica feature white paint with a black number, while the other cities in the Atacama Desert feature poles with yellow paint. Keep in mind the paint may have faded, making it look white.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Paint in the Desert
metas.note: Poles in Arica feature white paint with a black number, while the other cities in the Atacama Desert feature poles with yellow paint. Keep in mind the paint may have faded, making it look white.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Barichara Pavement
metas.note: This unique cobblestone pavement is found is the historic town of Barichara, Santander.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Barranquilla Roadbollard
metas.note: In Barranquilla, you can often find this bollard with roadnames on intersections.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Buenaventura Truck Spam Road
metas.note: The stretch of the 40 to Buenaventura is an important route for trucks, so if you see many trucks, it's worth a thought.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Caldas Polepaint
metas.note: orange & blue
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Cauca/Narino Polepaint
metas.note: Yellow with dark numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Coastal Antioquia Polepaint
metas.note: Green paint with yellow numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Electricity Counter - Oval
metas.note:
Usually pretty tall with oval windows, circle windows might not be as trustworthy.

Very common as there are few plastic counters in this region.
metas.footer: Source: The CoCo Document by Blinky

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - European Bollard
metas.note: This european-style (specifically spanish style bollard) is found in Cundinamarca, but also on the 40 towards Villavicencio.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - H-shaped lamp attachment
metas.note: H-shaped lamp attachment plates can be found in Bogota.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Huila Polepaint
metas.note: Orange paint with black numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Ibague Lamp
metas.note:
This red lamp style is unique to Tolima province.

Note by MB: I only found it in Ibague, not in any other towns in Tolima. Also, the meta is more about the color and the shape of the lamp, not about the arrangement of the lights.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Megabus
metas.note: Green or yellow, modern bus. Often on a dedicated bus lane. Found in Pereira metropolitan area.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Pole Marking - Antioquia
metas.note: These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - QR-Code Sticker
metas.note: Found in Barranquilla and Santa Marta
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Rectangular lamp attachment
metas.note: Rectangular lamp attachment plates can be found mainly in Medellin, sometimes further North, especially in Monteria and Cucuta.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Risaralda/Choco Polepaint
metas.note: Yellow paint with red numbers. Found all over Risaralda and the towns of Istmina and Quibdo in Choco.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Sarawak Pole
metas.note: Asymmetrical poles with a "Sarawak" extension (a vertical stalk coming out the top), can often be found East of Andes. Note that this pole is not 100%, and has been spotted elsewhere.
metas.footer: Source: Meat of the Day on ScripterCord

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Spikes
metas.note: These spikes can be found on the 40 and the 62.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Street Lamps - Barranquilla
metas.note: The uniquely shaped supporting metal piece can be found in Barranquilla. (Similar to the Providencia design)

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Street Lamps - Providencia
metas.note: Providencia street lights are green and supported by a trapezoidal sheet of metal underneath. (The metal sheet without a green lamp can also be found in Barranquilla)

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Tinto Bus
metas.note: This red bus drives in the town (not the country) Armenia.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Tolima Poletag
metas.note: Orange tag with white numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - TransLago vans
metas.note: TransLogo vans are common throughtout Boyaca Department. You will most often see them on the routes Tunja-Sogamoso and Tunja-Duitama.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Transmetro
metas.note: White Transmetro buses can be found in Barranquilla.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Tumaco
metas.note: If you see many puddles and a pavement out of '+' shaped stones, you're in Tumaco.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Valle de Cauca Pole
metas.note: If you see these poletops you will find yourself in Valle Del Cauca.
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Valle de Cauca Polepaint
metas.note: Yellow, with black numbers. Several digits can be in one row.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Villavicencio Bike Lane Road
metas.note: If you see a bike lane, and get East of Andes vibes, you're most likely on the road through Los Tobitos to Villavicencio.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Azure Blue Signpost
metas.note:
On the French Riviera (Côte d'Azur in French, literally translated as Blue Coast), you can find regular traffic signposts painted azure blue. Uniquely, Cagnes-sur-mer, west of Nice, will feature lighter, powder blue infrastructure.

NOTE: Blue infrastructure can be found to a lesser extent all across France, particularly Brittany, so consider the landscape as well.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Bordeaux Signpost
metas.note:
In the outskirts of Bordeaux, you may find square traffic signposts with the Bordeaux shade of red, named after the wine grown in the region.

NOTE: Red posts by themselves are not unique to Bordeaux, so apply this meta with caution.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Bordeaux Streetsign
metas.note: Small tables with 'Arrᵗ' written on a small separate sign, are found in Bordeaux, despite being a city not divided into arrondissements.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Brown Signback
metas.note:
Road signs where both the post and back are painted brown are most commonly found in Seine-et-Marne, and rarely in Ille-et-Vilaine. It is more reliable when the post is square, however round signposts are equally common.

NOTE: Beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Cityname Roadsign
metas.note:
Street signs in the metropolitan area of Paris often say the name of the city, which is generally atypical for street signs in France. The signs will often be made in a modern design, and many city names will be river based, notably named after Seine and Marne.

NOTE: This can be seen sporadically throughout the country, so consider other clues.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Cuboid Barrier
metas.note:
Cuboid barriers made of stones and mortar are commonly found on Corsica. While by no means unique to Corsica, it is good to consider the island when you see them in rounds with a plausible Mediterranean landscape.

NOTE: Stone barriers with a rounded top are not found on Corsica.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Dark Green Signpost
metas.note:
Dark green road signposts and backs are most commonly found in Brittany and around Paris, but also various southern regions in the country.

NOTE: Beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Eure-et-Loir Sticker
metas.note: Signbacks in Eure-et-Loir may include a green sticker, the department’s logo. They’re usually placed on a dark green back, without a matching post.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Grey Signback / Green Signpost
metas.note:
A greyish green signback supported by a darker green post, is found in three areas: Brittany (Côtes-d'Armor and eastern half of Ille-et-Vilaine), Pyrénées-Atlantiques and rarely near the Alps.

NOTE: Beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Lille Streetsign
metas.note: Street signs with a red slanted fleur-de-lis are unique to Lille.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Lyon Streetsign
metas.note:
Lyon’s street signs feature four corner bolts and an uninterrupted inner white border that cuts a notch for the arrondissement and each bolt.

NOTE: Outside Lyon proper, the street sign will display the name of the suburb instead.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Marseille Streetsign
metas.note: Marseille’s street signs will usually feature the city’s emblem, a variation of the Greek cross. The white border will usually be interrupted at the top, even when the cross is absent.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Montpellier Streetsign
metas.note: Montpellier street signs will typically contain a blue ‘M’ on a white background in the top left corner.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Paris Streetsign
metas.note:
Paris uses an iconic green & Prussian blue design with a top arch that has also been replicated in Bucharest, which is sometimes referred to as Paris of the east.

NOTE: The simple rectangular form of the sign can be found in the towns nearby and rarely in other cities.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Pas-de-Calais Sign
metas.note:
In the Pas-de-Calais department, you may find road signs with the following colour arrangement: a dark green post paired with a signback of a lighter shade of green, ranging from matcha green to greenish turquoise. The department’s logo, a green and blue triangle, is occasionally present on the signback.

NOTE: Under certain lighting, they can appear similar to the greyish road signs. Also, beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Powder Blue Infrastructure
metas.note: Uniquely, Cagnes-sur-mer, west of Nice, will feature lighter, powder blue infrastructure.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Reddish Road
metas.note:
Roads with a significant red, purple or burgundy tint are most commonly found in an area between Paris and Dijon, with Normandy being a notable exception. The historical region of Burgundy, which gave the name to the shade of red, roughly corresponds to the highlighted area.

NOTE: Normal roads may deceptively look reddish under some lighting, so use this with caution.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Thin B-Type Guardrail
metas.note:
Thin B type guardrail, typical for Czechia and Slovakia, is sometimes found on highways in the northern half of the country, often coming from Le Mans, Tours, Paris, Reims and Metz.

NOTE: On the highlighted sections, thin B can be the minority guardrail, and short sections of any highway will have no guardrails at all. It is also more common on smaller roads in the North, but less consistent as a clue.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Wind Turbine
metas.note: Wind turbines are considerably more common in the north of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Yellow Front License Plates
metas.note: France can sometimes have yellow back license plates, especially in old coverage. Should you see several yellow plates on the front, you're probably near Luxembourg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - ALDI Nord
metas.note: There are two regional Aldi chains, which have split Germany in two; Aldi Süd in the south, and Aldi Nord in the north.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - ALDI Süd
metas.note: There are two regional Aldi chains, which have split Germany in two; Aldi Süd in the south, and Aldi Nord in the north.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Black Disk Bollard
metas.note: Bollards standing on these black disks are commonly found in all of eastern Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Berlin
metas.note: Berlin uses segmented bus stops, with a yellow signpost.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Bremen
metas.note: Bremen proper uses simple bus stops, which have the bus stop name within a red section. The edges can be rounded.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Bremerhaven
