metas.note: Bremerhaven, which is still part of Bremen, uses bus stops with a grey section on the opposite side of the signpost. And the bus stop name is red within a yellow section.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Hamburg
metas.note: Hamburg bus stops have a red signpost, and the route numbers are within hexagons. Note that they can be found outside of Hamburg as well

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Capped Bollard
metas.note: Some bollards in North Rhine-Westphalia have a green bit at the top. The top can also be another colour.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Cologne Lamppost Plate
metas.note:
Lampposts in Cologne will often feature these bright yellow numbers on a black piece of plastic.

NOTE: Similar looking things can be found elsewhere as well.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Curved Poletop
metas.note: Pole tops which have a curved horizontal bar can be found in Bavaria, though they are rare.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Dark Reflector
metas.note: Bollards with darker reflectors than usual are commonly found in Schleswig-Holstein, Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Bavaria. They can sometimes be found in Baden-Württemberg and rarely in Hesse.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Double Connector Signback
metas.note: The double connector signback is very common in Schleswig-Holstein and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. It is also found in Brandenburg. Rarely, you may see it in Saxony, Rhineland-Palatinate or Hamburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Folded Sign
metas.note: Folded Signs are most common in Bremen, then Saxony-Anhalt and Saarland.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Grey Bollard Plate
metas.note: Baden-Württemberg is the only state where the plates on the bollards can be grey instead of white.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Lower Half Missing Bollard
metas.note: These irregular looking bollards, which do not have a white encasing on the bottom half, are found on K-roads in this region of Lower Saxony, around Lüneburg. K-Roads in this region will not have any other type of bollard.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Lower Saxony km Marker
metas.note: You can find these simple rectangular markers, with rounded edges in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - LVR Cap
metas.note: Some of the green caps will have the text ‘LVR’, along with a small coat of arms. These specific green caps are unique to southern North Rhine-Westphalia.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Metal Border km Marker - Lower Saxony
metas.note: These markers with a metallic border around the marker itself are found in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony. The numbers after the comma are usually smaller on the markers in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Metal Border km Marker - Schleswig-Holstein
metas.note: These markers with a metallic border around the marker itself are found in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony. The numbers after the comma are usually smaller on the markers in Lower Saxony (So if that's not the case go SchleHo)

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - No-Fold Signback
metas.note: Non-folded signbacks are most common in Schleswig-Holstein, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Hesse, Hamburg, Bremen, then Brandenburg, Saxony, Baden-Württemberg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Orange Bollard Plate
metas.note: Rhineland-Palatinate is the only state where the plates on the bollards are orange instead of white.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Orange Posts
metas.note: These simple orange posts are most commonly found in Bavaria, and also in the other highlighted states.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Red Bicycle Sign
metas.note: Red bicycle signs can be found in Northrhine-Westphalia, Southern Lower Saxony and Hamburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Red Cap Bollard
metas.note: These white posts with a red cap are found in all of former East Germany, but most commonly in the state of Saxony-Anhalt.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Round Concrete Poles
metas.note: These round concrete poles are almost unique to Former Eastern Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Saarland Bicycle Sign
metas.note: These dark-green designs can be found in Saarland only.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Schleswig-Holstein Bicycle Sign
metas.note: Schleswig-Holstein sometimes uses slightly different cycling sign designs. For the one with town-names, note the difference in the arrow. For the one without, the shape is different.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Berlin
metas.note: Berlin uses white signs with a grey border, and a separate section for numbers under the street name. Also note how the letter ß looks.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Darmstadt
metas.note: Streetsigns in Darmstadt are white and often are written in ALL CAPS, which is unique in Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Dortmund
metas.note: Dortmund uses blue signs with a white border and a grey frame. The signs also have a separate section for numbers under the street name.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Dresden
metas.note: Dresden has blue signs with a unique font.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Düsseldorf
metas.note: Düsseldorf has black signs with a white border, similar to Munich. The signs have a metallic frame.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Essen
metas.note: Essen has blue signs with a very thick metallic frame.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Frankfurt
metas.note: Frankfurt uses blue street signs with a metallic border around the sign, as well as the separate section for numbers under the street name.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Hanover
metas.note: Hanover uses white signs with a wider than usual gap between the sign and metallic frame.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Mainz
metas.note: Mainz has a mix of blue signs, and this unique red variant.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Munich
metas.note: Munich has blue street signs with a white decorative border that does not touch the corners. Also note the unique font.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Nuremberg
metas.note: Nuremberg has blue signs with a unique font. The signs also have a grey frame with a small gap between it and the sign.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Stuttgart
metas.note: Stuttgart uses black signs without a border.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Wuppertal
metas.note: Wuppertal uses white signs with a unique font and a white painted frame with a small gap between it and the sign.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - T-Signback
metas.note: The T-Signback is exclusive to Hamburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Thicc T Pole
metas.note: These pole tops where the middle of the horizontal bar is thicker can be found in all of former East Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Three Section Road Marker
metas.note: Bavaria uses these white rectangular road markers, which are divided by black lines into three sections. The left section provides the road you are currently on.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Trashcan - Berlin
metas.note: Berlin uses bright orange bins that have white text on them.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Trashcan - Bremen
metas.note: Bremen has green and grey bins, with orange speech bubbles.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Trashcan - Hamburg
metas.note: Hamburg uses bright red bins, with white speech bubbles.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Tree Tag
metas.note: Many trees in Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern have these tiny green markers on them. You can very rarely find them in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop
metas.note: Triangle pole tops are common in Western Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - Grey
metas.note: Baden-Württemberg uses grey triangle posts.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - North Rhine-Westphalia
metas.note: North Rhine-Westphalia uses white posts without white plates on the sides. You can also find posts which go all the way to the ground.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - Thuringia
metas.note: The plates on the Thuringia Triangle Posts are unique, as they have sections which are seperated by a black line.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - Unpainted
metas.note: Rhineland-Palatinate and Saxony use unpainted, rocky looking posts, with white plates stuck on each side.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - White
metas.note: Saarland, Thuringia, and Baden-Württemberg use white posts, with the same white plates attached. Note by MB: PlonkIt says they're smaller in BaWü. From what I saw, this is fake though.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Trident Poles
metas.note: These trident-like pole tops can be found in Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt, and Baden-Württemberg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Type A Guardrail
metas.note: I'd avise to learn where this cannot be found, which is Easter Germany, Hesse, Baden-Württemberg and Saarland.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Type B Guardrail
metas.note: I'd avise to learn where this cannot be found, which is Schleswig-Holstein, Rhineland-Palatinate, Bremen and Hamburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - White Bollard Plate
metas.note: These basic white plates on bollards can be found in all states except for Bavaria, Saarland and the City States.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - White Tree Paint
metas.note:
You can spot trees that are painted white close to the bottom of the trunk in the northeast.

NOTE: You will rarely find them outside the shaded region.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Wooden Bollard
metas.note: These round wooden bollards, which have a painted top, are found in Bavaria.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Yellow Bollard - No Plate
metas.note: Fully yellow posts are found in the state of Brandenburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Yellow Bollard - Plate
metas.note:
Yellow posts with a white plate on them are found in Saxony-Anhalt.

NOTE: Sometimes there is only 1 plate, which can make it hard to tell apart from a Brandenburg post.

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Elevated Railway
metas.note: The only elevated railway in Hawaii is on Oahu island and runs along the HI-99 for the most part, merges into the H-1 interstate and continues to the airport.

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - No Tab / Arrow
metas.note: No tab above sign, arrow on the actual sign, unique to Oahu.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - No Tab / No Arrow / Number
metas.note: Basic streetsigns, but with a number below the abbreviation (Rd/St/Pl/...), unique to Kauai.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - No Tab / No Number
metas.note: Basic streetsign, with only the road name, mostly found in Hawaii, rare on Kauai and extremely rare on Oahu and Maui.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - Tab (Empty)
metas.note: Tab above sign, but nothing in it, found in Maui district (which includes Maui, Lana'i and Moloka'i)
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - Tab / Long Arrow
metas.note: Tab above sign, containing a long arrow, found in Maui district (which includes Maui, Lana'i and Moloka'i)
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - Tab / Short Arrow
metas.note: Tab above sign, containing a short or very short arrow, almost unique to Oahu.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Iceland - Infrastructure - Divided Highway
metas.note: The 41 and 43 southwest of Reykjavík, as well as the 1 between Grundarhverfi and Selfoss are divided.

metas.name: Iceland - Infrastructure - Multi Lane Highway
metas.note: Both sides of the Hvalfjördur Tunnel have multiple lanes for one driving direction.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - ∀-Poletop
metas.note:
Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an upside down A (∀) slightly below the top of the pole.

94% Madhya Pradesh 2% Jharkhand 1% each: Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - <-Poletop
metas.note: Poles with two diagonal bars forming a ‘<’ shape are common in Meghalaya (75%) and Arunachal Pradesh (20%) and occasionally found in Assam (2%).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - 1 1/2 Trapezoids
metas.note: This pole configuraiton is mainly found in Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - ACC Cement
metas.note: Found everywhere except for North-East.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Ambuja Cement
metas.note: Commonly found everywhere, except for North East. Within North-East, it is sometimes found in Assam.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Andaman Black Sticker
metas.note:
These black paint can be circular or square, features 2 letters, an arrow beneath, and some numbers beneath that and can be on metal/concrete poles.

They're found mostly near the capital (Port Blair/Sri Vijaya Puram) (95%) and rarely near Diglipur (5%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Andaman Horizontal Bar Poletop
metas.note: Pole tops in Andaman mostly consist of horizontal bars perpendicular to the pole. They are not 100% unique to Andaman, but are very common there.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Antioquia Pole
metas.note: This black-yellow-black pole painting (which is famous for appearing in Antioquia in Colo), can also be found in Eastern Bihar along the Ganges.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Black & White Bollard
metas.note:
These bollards are rarer and not unique to Arunachal Pradesh, but if you think you are here, these are the areas these bollards are most commonly found

  • In Max West Arunachal Pradesh
  • North of Deed
  • North of Aalo
  • on the 319 in the East
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Divided Road
metas.note: The only divided road in Arunachal Pradesh is the NH415 south of Itanagar
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Pole Band
metas.note: A section of the NH13 west of Roing has poles marked with white numbers on blue, red or black paint.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Assam / West Bengal vans
metas.note: These vans (can be white, red, or orange) with specifically yellow plates, in NE India are found only within West Bengal and Assam. Doesn’t count with a white plate.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Assam Pavement
metas.note: Many roads in Assam are paved with these tiles. What makes it stand out is that it is also found on very rural roads.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Assam Trident Poles
metas.note: Trident poletops with the tip of the middle bar bent at a 90° angle can be found in Assam (98%).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bangur Cement
metas.note:
Bangur Cement is found in large parts of India.

It is only sometimes found in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi (where Bangur Power Cement) is more prevalent.

It is never found in

  • Kerala + Tamil Nadu
  • North East India
  • Gujarat
  • Anything North of Himachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bangur Power Cement
metas.note:
Found in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes also in Uttar Pradesh or Madhya Pradesh.

Don't confuse this with Bangur Cement, which has a different distribution.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bar underneath Generic Pole
metas.note:
Metal crossbar with no insulators

Most common in Maharahstra (50%)

Also occasionally found in other northern states.

Within the Northeast, it's exclusive to Tripura.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Big Ring Pole
metas.note:
Big rectangular metal ring around the pole.

Most common in Uttarakhand + Himachal Pradesh and Mizoram + Tripura.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bihar Pole + Mountains
metas.note: In Uttarakhand, the Bihar pole (yellow and black stripes) can be found on the NH109 North and a small road South of Dwarahat. Since Uttarakhand is mountainous, you shouldn't mistake it for Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bihar stripes
metas.note: Pole paint consisting of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes can be found in Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bihar/Jharkhand Guy
metas.note:
In Bihar and Jharkhand you will see many ads with this man with a turban and a beard. He's usually accompanied by a hexagonal company logo and a yellow background.

Note by MB: This sounds ridiculous but he seems to be so popular that there are copycats of him with the same Turban/beard style. So if you see a different company logo, don't trust this.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Black Tuk-Tuks
metas.note: Black Tuk-Tuks are most common in Maharashtra (maybe fake meta)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Blue & White Bridge
metas.note: The bridges in West Bengal frequently feature blue and white concrete blocks. It is also rarely found in Bihar around the city of Gaya.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Blue Pole Stickers
metas.note: These blue stickers on metal poles can be found on the NH109 near Lohali (UK)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Buddhism
metas.note:
Buddhist prayer flags and other Buddhist signals are mostly found in the Himalayas. Sometimes you can also find them in the Northeast, around Bangladesh, especially in Western Meghalaya, Western Mizoram and Southern Tripura. Rarely you can find it in central-eastern Maharashtra around Nagpur.

Note by MB: The colors in the map don't exactly match the text. The text is right though (for Geoguessr), not the map.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Lampe Circles
metas.note:
The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as round yellow markings on street lights.

NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Large Blue Signs
metas.note:
The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as blue signs mentioning sectors and industrial areas.

NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Streetsign
metas.note:
The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as street signs which will typically feature several numbers rather than street names.

NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh Poletop
metas.note:
Trident poletop, V-shaped bars underneath and Punjab Poletop.

Very hyperspecific for some roads in Chandigarh.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chennai Wall
metas.note: This wall pattern can be found in and around Chennai (but it is rare).
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chettinad Cement
metas.note: Recognizable by the C-Logo Found in South India, and sometimes in Goa and Maharashtra.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Combination of Even and Uneven Poletop
metas.note: In the northeast you may find poles with a combination of an even and uneven poletop.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Complicated Dark Metal Pole
metas.note:
Overly complicated, usually dark metal.

90% in West Bengal.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concrete Blocks
metas.note: Concrete blocks, similar to those you see in Bhutan, are commonly found in (but not limited to) North-East India
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concrete Holey Poles
metas.note:
Concrete holey poles are unique to Gujarat and the Union territory of Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Gujarat uses a variety of poletops, some of which can be used to identify other states. Beware that holey poles generally take precedence over poletop metas.

NOTE: They are rarely found in other states:

  • Maharashtra (2%)
  • Madhya Pradesh (1%)
  • Chhattisgarh (1%)
  • Odisha (0.5%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concrete Road / Yellow Lines
metas.note: From the city of Sukma to the border with Andra Pradesh, the NH30 has yellow road lines and is made of concrete. (Kinda similar to the famous Ruta 9 in Chile)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concreto Cement
metas.note: Found in East India (i.e. Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha)
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Dark Rock Walls
metas.note: Dark Rock Walls are commonly found around Udaipur, RJ.
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Dehradun Sticker
metas.note: These round white stickers can be found all over Dehradun (UK)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Delhi Bus
metas.note: Orange and bright green buses are typically found in Delhi.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Delhi stripes
metas.note:
Pole paint consisting of five or more thin black and yellow stripes can be found in Delhi.

#1 clue for rural Delhi (98%)

Has to be the exact order and color.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Delhi Yellow Sticker
metas.note: Besides Kerala and Uttarakhand, Delhi can also rarely have yellow stickers. All of these regions look very different.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Double Bull Cement
metas.note: Found in Central and East India, in Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes in Gujarat.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Duraguard Cement
metas.note:
Found in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chattisgarh, sometimes in Odisha.

Don't confuse with Duraton Cement.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Duraton Cement
metas.note:
Only found in Punjab and Jammu / Kashmir.

Don't confuse with Duraguard Cement.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Elevated Jharkhand Structures
metas.note: These elevated structures are found a lot of them between Hazaribagh and Ranchi in Jharkhand.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Extended Vertical Bar
metas.note:
Extra vertical bar at the top of the pole, extends significantly over the pole.

85% West Bengal 12% Chhattisgarh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Generic Poletop
metas.note: Typically not south of Maharashtra-Chhattisgarh-Odisha except in Kerala. Generic pole does NOT include any bars on the top of pole
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Generic Poletop with Grey Crossbar
metas.note:
If the generic poletop has a grey crossbar, you're most likely in Uttar Pradesh. It's less commonly found in Odisha, Bihar, and more rarely in Haryan and Jharkhand.

If it's in South India, it's 98% Kerala.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Goa Poletops
metas.note:
This poletop has two crossbars, the top one is short with 2 insulators, the bottom one is long with 4 insulators.

It's mostly found in Goa (95%) and rarely in Kerala (2%), Maharashtra (1%) and Karnataka (1%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Green Pole Stripes
metas.note: Green pole stripes are commonly found in the far western roads of Arunachal Pradesh. They are often combined with yellow or white stripes.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Gujarat - Non-Holey Pole
metas.note: Almost all poles in Gujarat are holey poles. Generic poles are only found sometimes in very far west Gujarat, near the border with Pakistan
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Harsil Road
metas.note: On the road south of Harsil (UK), you will find a large amount of poles with red/yellow stripes and black bollards with stripes (see UK/JH bollard)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - HiBond Cement
metas.note: Recognizable by the wavy triangle logo. Found only in Gujarat.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Himachal Pradesh - Double Guardrail
metas.note: The NH5 near Sarahan ist the only road in Himachal Pradesh with a double guardrail.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Hollow Metal Pole
metas.note:
This means, it has an indent that runs through the whole pole. If you look at it from the top, it looks like a C.

Most common in Mizoram, seen in Himachal Pradesh as well.

Note by MB: Seen this in central states too, but still useful together with landscape ig.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Hyderabad Mesh Pole
metas.note:
Mesh pole with three wires on one or both sides, that are connected to the pole in a "pyramid shaped" extension on the side.

Note that it has to be a pole, not a cellphone tower (which would be a lot larger).

Found around Hyderabad, TG
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - JK Lakshmi Cement
metas.note:
Found in North and Central India, plus Jharkhand, Odisha and Gujarat. Sometimes also in Maharashtra.

Don't confuse with JK Power Cement (which hasn't been researched yet).
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - JSW Cement
metas.note: Found in South India, Goa + Maharashtra, and Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Karnataka Pole
metas.note:
In Karnataka (85%), and sometimes in Haryana (6%), Western Andhra Pradesh (6%) and rarely Uttar Pradesh (1%), you can find trident poletops on concrete poles where the central insulator is attached directly to the top of the pole, while the other two are attached to a horizontal crossbar positioned slightly further down. There are different variants of this poletop that increase the likelihood for Karnataka.

Note by MB: Make sure not to confuse it with the trident with a small bar at the top (see images).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Karnataka Pole - Karnataka Insulator
metas.note:
If a trident pole has these insulators with three circles and air between them, it is found 98% in Karnataka.

The other versions of this poletop have lower certainties for Karnataka.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala "Weird" Poletop
metas.note: Made of metal, has a "generic" crossbar, but additionally a very long bar that extends into one direction at the top, which holds the actual insulators.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala Bollard
metas.note: What makes these bollards unique is the red reflector on a stone bollard.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala Bridge
metas.note: Blue and white bridges can commonly be found all over Kerala. They can sometimes be painted in green.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala Yellow Marker
metas.note:
Small yellow pole markings are commonly found in Kerala.

Can also be used to rule out Kerala since 80-90% of all poles have it.

Can also be found in Goa (2-3%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Konark Cement
metas.note: Found in Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Large Rectangle
metas.note: In West Bengal you may also find poletops containing two crossbars which are connected to each other with thin vertical supports on either side. The lower bar is connected on either side to the pole with diagonal supports.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - License Plates - Andhra Pradesh
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

AP stands for Andhra Pradesh.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - License Plates - Karnataka
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

KA stands for Karnataka.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - License Plates - Kerala
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

KL stands for Kerala.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Madhya Pradesh - Rock Walls
metas.note: In Madhya Pradesh, rock walls are very common around two national parks : Kuno National Park and Panna National Park
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Maharashtra Pole
metas.note:
This pole is either metal or concrete (but more skinny than a generic pole). It has one or two small bars near the poletop.

It's not exclusive to Maharashtra, but very common there.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Manipur Poletop
metas.note: In Manipur you can often find trident poletops on poles made entirely out of metal. They sometimes have small bars on the top of the trident.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Max Cement
metas.note: Found only in North-East India, but not in Nagaland or Arunachal Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Meghalaya - Divided Road
metas.note:
The NH6 north of Shillong is the only divided highway in Meghalaya.

Note by MB: A good way to tell you're in Meghalaya is the lack of non-latin scripts.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Metal Holey Poles
metas.note: Metal holey poles are common in Kerala.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Metal Mesh Poles
metas.note: Metal poles with a mesh pattern are commonly found in Sikkim (93%) and rarely in Arunachal Pradesh (5%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Mycem Cement
metas.note: Found only in Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Nagaland Auto
metas.note: Auto Rickshaws with a Black Body and a Yellow Roof (i.e. reverse to the Andhra Pradesh / Telangana variant) are commonly found in Nagaland.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - NH51 / Gujarat
metas.note: The NH51 in Gujarat is unique because it is lined with many dark metal poles (unlike most of Gujarat which has concrete holey poles). It is also divided and paved with concrete.
metas.footer: Source: bibberbang1234 on the LearnableMeta Discord + additional self research

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Odisha Bridge
metas.note: Some bridges in Odisha are made of green and white concrete blocks as guardrails
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Orange Pole Paint
metas.note: This Orange Pole Paint is found on the NH15 in Arunachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Orange Pole Stickers
metas.note: These orange stickers on metal poles can be found in Uttarakhand, mostly in the East.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Painted Stripes
metas.note: Metal poles in Uttarakhand sometimes have those red or yellow stripes painted on them.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Pole with Black/White bottom
metas.note:
White and black stripes on the bottom of a pole are found in both Meghalaya and Tripura.

Note by MB: Don't confuse this with the Tamil Nadu polepainting, which is always white-black-white and further up on the pole.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Pole with Red Paint
metas.note:
Silver painted poles with a red or brown top.

Common in Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh, sometimes Tripura & Mizoram.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Punjabi Electricity Counters
metas.note: Electricity counters in Punjab are usually mint green with small window-like squares. They can rarely be seen in Haryana.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Pure Metal in Uttarakhand
metas.note: In the Himalayas, pure metal poles are usually more common in the North-East. If you see them in the Northwest, it's most likely Uttarakhand.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rajasthan - Rock Walls / Flat Landscape
metas.note: Rock walls are not unique to Rajasthan, but if you know or have a feeling you’re in Rajasthan, it is most common south of Udaipur (hilly) and southeast of Kota (flat). This can be used combined with the elevation to get the precise area.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rajasthan - Rock Walls / Flat Landscape
metas.note: Rock walls are not unique to Rajasthan, but if you know or have a feeling you’re in Rajasthan, it is most common south of Udaipur (hilly) and southeast of Kota (flat). This can be used combined with the elevation to get the precise area.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rajasthan Mesh Pole
metas.note:
Found 90% in Rajasthan.

Sikkim and Telangana also have Mesh poles, but they're different.

The Sikkim pole is slimmer, while the Telangana pole has "triangles" at the top.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Ramco Cement
metas.note: Found in South India, however less common in Karnataka. Sometimes also found in West Bengal.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Red & White Bollard
metas.note: It is quite rare to see red and white bollards, but they are mostly found in far west Arunachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Red&White Tree Paint
metas.note: In Bihar, and less commonly Jharkhand, you may find trees with four red and white stripes painted near the bottom.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rusted Hollow Pole
metas.note: Thin rusted Poles that are hollow, i.e. have an indent going from the bottom to the top, are found in Maharashtra, and sometimes in Chhattisgarh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Sanghi Cement
metas.note: Recognizable by the Lion Logo. Found only in Gujarat.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Seperated Bus Lane
metas.note: On large roads in Ahmedabad and Surat you can find separated middle lanes for buses. Beware that people will still often drive in these lanes.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Shree Cement
metas.note: Found everywhere, except for Himalayan states, North Eastern States, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Sikkim Taxis
metas.note: Taxis in Sikkim often have a painted yellow hood or a small yellow circle on it.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Simple Black Sticker
metas.note:
This black sticker usually just has few characters, often just a number.

35% Tamil Nadu 35% Andhra Pradesh 20% Telangana

Note that it's a weak meta for Andhra over Telangana.

Do not confuse for Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Small Extra Bar
metas.note:
Short bar at the top of the pole.

Mostly in Rajasthan and Telangana Sometimes Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra Rarely Jharkhand.

In the Northeast, it can be found in Tripura or rarely in Arunachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Small Ring Pole
metas.note:
Very similar to a second vertical bar, but it is attached to the pole on its ends, rather than in the middle, giving it a ring shape. What differentiates it from the big ring pole is that the bar isn't far away from the pole.

35% Maharashtra 35% Madhya Pradesh 20% Chhattisgarh 2% Rajasthan & Mizoram 1% Tripura
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Small Trapezoid
metas.note:
Trapezoid poletop, but the diagonal bars do not reach the end of the crossbar.

Most common in flat Arunachal Pradesh Sometimes in Tripura
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Square Stick Fences
metas.note:
In the northeast you will commonly see fences made of thin wooden sticks in a square pattern.

They can also sometimes be seen in Odisha, which has a very different landscape, making it useful to distinguish Odisha from other eastern states.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Star Cement
metas.note: Found in North-East India, West Bengal and sometimes Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Symmetric Trident / Asymmetric Insulators
metas.note:
60% Tamil Nadu 20% Telangana 15% Andhra Pradesh

Important that the crossbar is symmetric, if it's asymmetric, it's usually TG.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - T-shaped Pole Extension
metas.note:
This pole extensions (above the pole) with 3 insulators

45% Andhra Pradesh 45% Telangana 9% Tamil Nadu
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tall, Narrow Rectangle Poletop
metas.note: A variety of poletops attached to the pole with two vertical bars forming a tall and narrow rectangle can be found in West Bengal.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tamil Nadu Pole
metas.note:
3 insulators in a horizontal line, or middle insulator slightly above others

88% Tamil Nadu 5% Bihar 3% Haryana 2% Uttar Pradesh 1.5% Andhra Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole
metas.note: In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Bars in different directions
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If the bars point in different directions, it's often in Meghalaya.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Dark Metal / Single Bar
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If it's a single bar, with dark metal, it's 80% Meghalaya 15% Assam
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Grey Metal
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If the pole is made out of bright/grey metal, it's 45% Meghalaya 45% Assam
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Poles - Dark Metal / Double Bar
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If it's dark metal and has two bars, it's 65% Meghalaya 15% Assam 15% Mizoram
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - TG/AP Bridge
metas.note: Bridges in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh are often recognizable by the color of their guardrails. It is often made of vertical red/pink/orange concrete blocks with horizontal white/light yellow blocks.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thai Bollards
metas.note: "Thai" bollards (white-black-white) are found in Odisha.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thick Grey Trapezoid
metas.note:
Commonly found in Kerala (especially with yellow stickers).

Note that there's also a version with the two indents, which is not found in Kerala, but in Andhra Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thick Trapezoid - Two Indents
metas.note:
Thick gray trapezoid, with two indents in the pole material.

97% Andhra Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thin Grey Metal Poles
metas.note: Thin grey metal poles are seen all over northeastern India and in the Himalayan region of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. You will commonly see two of these poles in close proximity.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tiny Crossbar
metas.note: A pole with no poletop except for this tiny bar, is often found in Odisha (70-80%)
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Toothbrush + Horizontal Bar
metas.note:
Insulators at the top, directly attached to the concrete, pointing in one direction. Below, there is a metal crossbar with no insulators.

70% Maharashtra 10% Chhattisgarh 5% Himachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Trapezoid - Dark Metal
metas.note:
Trapezoid poletops with poles completely made out of dark metal, are found in Chhattisgarh 95% of the time.

If it's not made out of dark metal, it's less certain.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Trapezoid Pole (Concrete)
metas.note:
A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down trapezoid.

80% Chhattisgarh 10% Maharashtra 3% Karnataka 2% Odisha 1% each: Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam

NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present. Northeast India also has some trapezoid poletops that look a bit different.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop
metas.note: Upside down triangle poletops placed below the top of the pole are commonly found in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and less commonly in Madhya Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop / Dumbbell Insulators
metas.note: 32% Maharashtra 32% Madhya Pradesh 32% Chattisgarh 1% Andhra Pradesh 1% Telangana
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop & Three Insulators
metas.note:
Triangle poletops with three insulators on top can be found in Jammu and Kashmir, sometimes in Himachal Pradesh.

Note: Do not confuse this with the regular triangle poletops which can be found elsewhere. Also even these poletops are not 100% unique to J&K
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Window
metas.note:
Triangle-shaped window insulators on a crossbar.

90% Jharkhand 2% Chhattisgarh 1% Bihar
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Trident / Asymmetric Bar
metas.note:
This pole has an asymmetric crossbar, with one side double the length of the other, and two insulators on the longer side, and one on the shorter side.

Research is not conclusive due to its rarity, but it's estimated to be 95% Telangana.

Note by MB: It's important that the bar is asymmetric, if it's symmetric, and the insulators are asymmetric, it's a different pole.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triple Karnataka Poletop
metas.note:
Concrete Trident pole with three crossbars.

Do not confuse it with the North-Eastern Triple Poletop, which has shorter crossbars and is made out of metal instead of concrete.

Found 98% in Karnataka 0.5% in Gujarat
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tripura Pole
metas.note: Tripura Poles often tend to have an extra bar underneath as well as the small crossbar on top.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Two Section Pole - High Bar
metas.note:
Two-section poles can sometimes be regionguessed by looking at the bar above the crossbar (which doesn't always exist).

If it's high on the pole (meaning you can barely see the concrete above it), it's 80% Telangana, 20% Andhra Pradesh (especially western)

Sometimes it's hard to tell though, so it can be a bit of a cope
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Two Section Pole - Low Bar
metas.note:
Two-section poles can sometimes be regionguessed by looking at the bar above the crossbar (which doesn't always exist).

If it's lower on the pole (meaning you can see a bit of concrete over the bar), it's 85% Andhra Pradesh, 15% Telangana

Sometimes it's hard to tell though, so it can be a bit of a cope
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Two Section Poles
metas.note: Poles divided in two sections, in a similar fashion to Brazilian poles, are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - UK/JH Bollard
metas.note: This black bollard with stripes (usually at least one of the colors: red, white, orange) can be found in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Ultra Tech Cement
metas.note: Can be found anywhere except for North-East India.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Uttarakhand - Red/white pole paint
metas.note: In Uttarakhand, you can find these red-white stripes on poles on random roads around Dwarahat.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Vertical Bar
metas.note:
Vertical bar at the poletop. It is attached to the pole with two short bars. Note that those bars are not at the end of the vertical bar, which would make it a ring pole (and change the distribution)

50% Chhattisgarh 30% Madhya Pradesh 15% Maharashtra 10% West Bengal
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Vertical Insulators
metas.note:
3-5 Insulators pointing upwards, attached to the pole.

Common in Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, sometimes Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - West Bengal E-Rickshaw
metas.note: West Bengal only has E-Rickshaws. They have a unique shape and are often blue.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - White Metal Plate
metas.note:
Can sometimes be rusted and a bit more brown.

Found in Northern States: Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar, sometimes Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - White-Black-White Paint
metas.note:
Markings on poles and trees, consisting of one black stripe in-between two white ones, are common in Tamil Nadu.

Note by MB: This only counts if it's black, not with other colors.

99.3% Tamil Nadu 0.02% Andhra Pradesh 0.01% Madhya Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt &India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Windfarms
metas.note:
The places with the most wind farms are indeed Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. This is pretty advanced knowledge, but region guessing states can be possible by learning where wind farms are:

  • Gujarat: Southwestern half
  • Karnataka: Davanagere to Hubballi
  • Tamil Nadu: Max South; Around Coimbatore
  • Maharashtra: Tristate to Madhya and Gujarat; Around Jath (southern)
  • Rajasthan: Jodhpur to Jaisalmer
  • Madhya Pradesh: West & North of Indore
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Window Poletop
metas.note: Small metal poletops in the shape of a window are found in Punjab and Haryana. 93% Punjab 4% Haryana 1% Delhi & Jammu (on Punjabi border) 0.5% Rajasthan 0.2% Ladakh
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Wonder Cement
metas.note: Found Northwest of Madhya Pradesh, however not in Himachal Pradesh or further North.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Outer Lines
metas.note:
Parts of roads NH6 and NH206 southeast of Shillong can be recognised by the presence of khasi pines with distinct yellow outer road lines and fresh dark pavement.

NOTE: This is the only road in Meghalaya that uses yellow outer road lines, but these lines exist in other states as well.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Bands
metas.note: Between Aizawl and Champhai on the NH6, poles will have yellow bands.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Stickers
metas.note: These orange stickers on metal poles can be found in Uttarakhand, mostly in the East.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Tuk Tuk / Black Roof
metas.note:
Yellow tuk tuks with black roofs are common in the southern Indian states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

NOTE: They can also rarely be found elsewhere.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Zuari Cement
metas.note: Found in South India, especially in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrasturcutre - Karnataka Symmetrical Poletop
metas.note:
2 insulators on each side, with the top of the pole sticking out.

Found in Karnataka (94%) and rarely in Tamil Nadu (4%) or Kerala (1%)
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Cigarette Blocks
metas.note: Central Sulawesi features these unique bollards that are painted black on the bottom, white in the middle, and yellow on the top.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Even Pole
metas.note: Indonesia uses two types of pole tops: even and uneven. This refers to the bar that holds the insulators and whether it is symmetrical to the pole itself. Knowing where even and uneven poles are most commonly found is useful for region guessing.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Green Bridge
metas.note: Green paint can often be seen on the side of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Indented Pole
metas.note: Poles with an indent on both sides are found in West Java, Jakarta, and Banten.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - North Sumatra Pole
metas.note: These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Nusa Pole
metas.note: On the Lesser Sunda Islands ('Nusas'), you can find poles with an extra long support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Pole Tape
metas.note: You can often see thin, black poles next to regular poles near the East Peninsula of Central Sulawesi. Two pieces of tape can be seen near the top of the poles, usually light blue and green. These can rarely be seen in northern South East Sulawesi.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Rectangle Attachment
metas.note: Bali features both even and uneven poles, as well as the Lesser Sunda island variants. You can also find this unique rectangle attachment on the pole tops in Bali.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Sulawesi Fences
metas.note: These painted fences are typically found on Sulawesi. They will be mostly painted white with blue or red.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Surabaya Pavement
metas.note: Pavement made out of bricks like this is found in East Java, particularly around Surabaya

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Trapezoid Pole
metas.note: Pole tops in North and Central Sulawesi, and Gorontalo commonly feature an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Triangle Attachment
metas.note:
You can find these poles with a triangle attachment under the horizontal bar in the following regions.

NOTE: This does not apply to stacked poles.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Trident Pole
metas.note: Trident style pole tops are most commonly found in Central Java and Yogyakarta, and rarely in South and West Kalimantan, and North Sumatra and Riau.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Uneven Pole
metas.note: Indonesia uses two types of pole tops: even and uneven. This refers to the bar that holds the insulators and whether it is symmetrical to the pole itself. Knowing where even and uneven poles are most commonly found is useful for region guessing.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 29 in Ad Dhakhiliyah
metas.note: The southern section of Road 29 only has a middle white line, which along with the greyish and sandy desert landscape makes this road unique.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 31 (divided)
metas.note: The divided section of Road 31 is the only divided road going through a flat desert landscape.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 31 (single lane)
metas.note: This long stretch of Road 31 can be recognised by the light-coloured flat desert landscape along with the wide shoulders and the often faded road lines. The weather is usually somewhat cloudy.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 37 (Powerline)
metas.note: Road 37 travels in a generally northwest direction through a very generic, flat desert landscape. The angle is one of the best clues for this road. On the southern half, a big power line is visible to the northeast.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 39 (flat)
metas.note: Road 39 is also one of the more generic roads. Probably the best way to recognise it are the narrow, or even non-existent shoulders.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 39 (hilly)
metas.note: Road 39 is also one of the more generic roads. Probably the best way to recognise it are the narrow, or even non-existent shoulders. The western parts can get quite hilly

metas.name: Infrastructure - 42 north of Shalim
metas.note: North of Shalim Road 42 turns into a very wide unpaved road, with the soil being quite light in colour. You’ll sometimes see oil drills in the distance along this stretch.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bin Color - Black
metas.note:
Black Bins can be found everywhere except for Batina North. They're also rarely found in South-Dhakiliyah.

NOTE: Even the dark blue and red regions are not 100% a certain colour.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bin Color - Grey
metas.note:
Grey Bins can be found in Dharihar, South Dhakhiliyah, Dhofar, Bathina North and west of Muscat.

NOTE: Even the dark blue and red regions are not 100% a certain colour.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / Black Sticker
metas.note: Black bins with a black sticker on the front can be found in Al Buraimi, Ash Sharqiyah North, and Muscat Governorates.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / No Sticker
metas.note:
Black bins without stickers are mainly found in Al Batinah South Governorate and north of Al Khaburah in Al Batinah North Governorate.

NOTE: Black bins throughout Oman may appear like they lack stickers, so use this with caution.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / White Sticker
metas.note: Black bins with a white sticker are found in Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate, southern Dhofar Governorate, and Muscat Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Western Bin
metas.note: Western-style small black bins are found in Muscat and eastern Al Batinah North Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chevron Bin
metas.note:
Bins in Muscat governorate often have white-and-red chevron-like stickers on the sides.

Note by MB: 'often' really is an overstatement, definitely don't rule Muscat out if you don't have those stickers.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Fahud Road
metas.note: The road west of Fahud goes through a flat desert with pink-greyish soil. The road itself is in poor shape and without roadlines as well as the direction of the road being southeast.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / Black Sticker
metas.note: Grey bins with a black sticker on the front are found in Ad Dhahirah Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / No Sticker
metas.note:
Grey bins without a sticker on the front are found in Al Batinah North Governorate.

NOTE: They can have a sticker on the side.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / White Sticker
metas.note: Grey bins with a white sticker are commonly found in Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate, and sometimes in Dhofar Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Ibri Road
metas.note: The road going to Saudi Arabia from Ibri can be recognised by the completely flat desert landscape with bright pink-greyish soil along with the road having very wide shoulders and the overall great road condition. The southern portion goes in a straight northeast direction, and the northern section curves more and can have more shrubs.

metas.name: Infrastructure - License Plates - Assam
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

AS stands for Assam.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: Infrastructure - License Plates - Maharashtra
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

MH stands for Maharashtra.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: Infrastructure - North of Ubar Road
metas.note: The unlabelled road northwest of Ubar can be recognised by the small white markings between the dashes.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Oil Drills
metas.note: Oil drills are common around Amal and sometimes seen along Road 39.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road to Yemen
metas.note: Just west of ميتان, only labelled in Arabic on Google Maps, literally translating to methane, there is a stretch of road, which has a uniquely light-coloured pavement. To the north, you can see sand dunes.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road west of Ubar
metas.note: West of Ubar, the 43 and the unlabelled road west of it are still unpaved but now have a power line to the north. The desert landscape has an orange tint to it.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Side Sticker
metas.note: Regardless of colour, if the bins have a sticker on the side, you should be in one of the North Coast governorates.

metas.name: Infrastructure - signpost with yellow sticker
metas.note: Signposts in the Northern Territory can feature these yellow stickers.

metas.name: Infrastructure - South-East of Ubar Road
metas.note:
The road southeast of Ubar has a general northwest bound angle, along with a power line to the left of the road. You will often see signs of life in the form of farms or buildings on this road.

NOTE: Don’t mix this up with the 37, which has a similar angle, but is more desolate and can have sunset coverage.

metas.name: Infrastructure - State Flag - Arizona
metas.note: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.name: Infrastructure - State Flags
metas.note: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow
metas.note: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Bolts
metas.note: This arrow, found in the Aomori prefecture (or more rarely Hokkaido), has distinct silver bolts around the border.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Long
metas.note: This variation, found in the Gifu prefecture, is long and thin.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Northern 275
metas.note: This alternate yellow and black design can often be found on the northern part of National Highway 275 in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Yellow/Black
metas.note: This yellow and black arrow can be found on Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Yellow/Green
metas.note: This yellow and green arrow is found southwest of Sapporo.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Birch Poles
metas.note: These artistically painted poles, made to resemble birch trees, are unique to the city of Date in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Akita
metas.note: This bollard, much like Tohoku, will be a thick, white bollard with an octagonal reflector. However, this Akita prefecture variation will have two yellow stripes underneath the reflector.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Aomori
metas.note: This bollard, found in the Aomori prefecture, has two yellow stripes, a single circular reflector, and is extendable. Sometimes, only one thicker stripe near the top may be present.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Black Stripe
metas.note: Some bollards on the island of Shikoku can have a black stripe just under the reflector. They can be found normally, attached to guardrails or walls.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Extendable
metas.note: In the northern parts of the Chugoku region, you can primarily find these basic snow poles, with either a thin extended, or thin contracted top. They can also sometimes be found in Iwate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Okoyama
metas.note: This bollard, with an octagonal reflector, and red stripe underneath it, is exclusive to the Okayama prefecture. Additionally, there will be a sloped connection where the base meets the reflector.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Orange Reflector
metas.note:
This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a series of separated orange reflectors on one side, and the same white on the opposite.

NOTE: Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Striped / No Reflector
metas.note: These striped bollards (which cover over the original) have a thinner top half, and no reflectors, and are common to the Tohoku region. They are especially common in Akita prefecture.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Tohoku
metas.note: This thick, white bollard, found in the Tohoku region, will have an octagonal reflector, and yellow stripe just underneath. In addition, you can find the same bollard, but with a rectangular top.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Tohoku (Black Variant)
metas.note: Additionally to regular Tohoku bollards, there are two other variations. You can find a black octagonal, and rectangular version. They are often found on National Highways or Expressways and can have the number printed on them.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Toyama
metas.note:
The Toyama prefecture bollard has one reflector, is extendable and has a red stripe underneath the reflector.

NOTE: Be careful: if there is either a second reflector, or a yellow stripe instead of a red one, these are different bollards. These are more common variations found across many prefectures.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Claymore
metas.note: Kerosine tanks, otherwise known as “Claymores”, can be found more commonly the further north you go. They are abundant in Hokkaido, but can be found in prefectures south of it, or in high elevation mountainous areas.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Ehime Cycling Route
metas.note:
Cycling routes in Ehime use an outside white, with an inside blue line. They are more commonly found along the coast but may be found further inland too.

While exceptions do exist, and can be found in other prefectures, they are the extreme minority.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Gas Tank
metas.note:
Hot water, gas and propane tanks can be found more frequently in northern prefectures or high elevation mountainous areas. Here are a few common variations you can find:

  • The standard hot water tank.

  • Covered propane tanks.

  • Exposed propane tanks.

  • These cylindrical tanks.

  • And finally, these circular tripod tanks.

Moreover, these are even more common in rural towns or villages, where major water or gas lines are unavailable.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Green Band
metas.note: Green bands on guardrails are most commonly found in Oita and Miyazaki, but can be found on all of Kyushu.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Hokkaido Sticker
metas.note:
You can find these chevron-like stickers, or more rarely orange ones, on guardrails in Hokkaido.

  • On the end or side of a guardrail.

  • Stuck to metal posts between wire fences, which are often found in Hokkaido.

  • On railings, which are often found on bridges, underneath the inside of the railing.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Red-Yellow Stripes

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - 2 or 3 Insulators
metas.note:
The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.

NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Black Tap Connector
metas.note: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black “tap” connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Cross (Chugoku Variant)
metas.note: The transformers in Chugoku, which have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a full triangle, will have a long horizontal or short vertical insulator(s) at the end.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Cross (Hat Insulator)
metas.note: The transformers in Shikoku, which also have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a half triangle, will have “hat shaped” short horizontal insulators at the end.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Insulator Box
metas.note: These grey “insulator-esque” blocks, which wires are fed through, can be found in the regions of Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku, Shikoku, and very rarely in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Kyushu
metas.note: The transformers in Kyushu, which have a straight bar attached on the side of the pole with three insulators at the end, will have transformers mounted 180-degrees from one another.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Lamp-Shaped Insulator
metas.note:
The transformers in Hokuriku, which are attached with thin metal bars, often have these small “lamp” shaped insulators. There will never be a bar present except for the attachment mentioned above.

NOTE: The prefecture of Niigata will have the Tohoku transformer design, as opposed to Hokuriku one.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Metal Bracket
metas.note: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black “tap” connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Okinawa
metas.note: Transformers in Okinawa, which have a T-shaped bar attached on the side of the pole, will have transformers mounted on opposite sides of the pole.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - One on Square
metas.note:
In Tohoku, you may also find transformers mounted on the side of a square, with a straight bar mounted on the top of the square. Rarely, you may find a square without a bar.

NOTE: While Kansai may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the bottom rather than the top.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Plus-Shaped Bar
metas.note: The electrical poles in Hokkaido either have this plus-shaped bar attached to the side of the pole, or one transformer mounted on two bars.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Red Number
metas.note: In Chugoku, a white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with red numbers. They may also be painted on the side.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Round Plate / T-Bar
metas.note:
The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.

NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Round Plate / Zigzag Bar
metas.note: The transformers in Tohoku, which often have additional square holding brackets and the logo of the Tohoku Electrical Company, are sometimes mounted on a round plate with a zigzag bar.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Square / Bottom Bar
metas.note:
The transformers in Kansai have either a straight or zigzag bar mounted on the bottom of a square. The transformer(s) will be mounted on the sides of that same square.

While this is uncommon, the bar and transformer(s) may be mounted on a vertical bar, rather than a square.

NOTE: While Tohoku may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the top rather than the bottom

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Triangle
metas.note: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black “tap” connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Two Bars
metas.note: The electrical poles in Hokkaido either have this plus-shaped bar attached to the side of the pole, or one transformer mounted on two bars. The Kanto Transformer may also be mounted on two bars.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Two on Square
metas.note: In Hokkaido, if there is more than one transformer, they will often be mounted on the sides of a square.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - White Sticker
metas.note: A white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with black numbers.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Wooden Plate
metas.note:
The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.

NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Chubu
metas.note: This tuning fork pole top, with a short top bar and horizontal bar below, is found the majority of the time in the Chubu region.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Kansai
metas.note: This tuning fork pole top, with a thin wire and horizontal bar below, is common in the Kansai region.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Kanto
metas.note: This tuning fork pole top, with a long top bar that sticks out each end and horizontal bar(s) below, is found the majority of the time in the Kanto region.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Vertical Traffic Light
metas.note: Vertical traffic lights can be found in Hokkaido, and along the northwestern coast. The usual horizontal traffic lights can be found everywhere else.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Yellow Circle Sign
metas.note: These specific black signs with two yellow circles are found in Kagawa. Other variations can be seen, including them stacked on top of each other, or with an arrow attached above.
