metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Asymmetric & Double-Stacked Insulator
metas.note: Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Black Tar
metas.note:
Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line can be seen in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero.

NOTE: This is most reliable when the tar is not faded.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Blue Grain Pavement
metas.note:
Grainy pavement with a blue-ish grey tinge is a common sight for the states of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.

NOTE: In Tamaulipas, larger roads very commonly feature dashed outer lines.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Cancun Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with five circular bulbs that looks like a dice is found in Cancun.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - CDMX Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in and around Mexico City have a white lower half with a pink upper half.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Chihuahua Cross
metas.note: A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Chihuahua Pole Paint
metas.note: Poles in Chihuahua city occasionally have a strip of white pole paint with the street name written in black or blue text.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Cobblestone
metas.note: This style of cobblestone pavement, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Cuernavaca Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a black rectangular head is found in Cuernavaca.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Durango Pole
metas.note: Poles with a lowered crossbar and a single support beam that extend from one end of the crossbar to the pole itself can be found in Durango.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Eurus Wind Farm
metas.note: The Eurus Wind Farm is located in southeast Oaxaca and is the largest wind farm in Mexico. Rows of wind turbines can be found along the 190 around Juchitán de Zaragoza.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Green Bottom Pole
metas.note:
The bottom half of poles in Cuernavaca are often painted green.

NOTE: In Generation 4, the paint usually looks faded, some to the point where it is barely visible.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Hanging Insulator (Concrete)
metas.note: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Hanging Insulator (Wooden)
metas.note: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Hexagonal Tiles
metas.note: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Jalisco Bollard
metas.note: Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text ‘Jalisco’ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Light Rock Wall
metas.note: These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Matamoros Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a rectangular head and a ring-shaped light bulb is found in Matamoros.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Mesh Pole
metas.note: Poles with a mesh body are most commonly found in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Nayarit Bollard
metas.note: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Oaxaca Pavement
metas.note: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is exclusive to Oaxaca.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Santiago de Queretaro Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with black front and back edges and a white middle section is found in Santiago de Queretaro.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Tree Fences
metas.note:
These fences made out of trees with red-coloured bark are commonly found in Veracruz.

NOTE: These tree fences can still be found in other coastal states and are best utilised when combined with other clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - White Acorn Insulator
metas.note: White insulators that are shaped like acorns can be found along the coastal states of Mexico, but are by far most common in Michoacan, Colima, and Veracruz.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - White Roadlines
metas.note: White middle roadlines are most commonly found in Tabasco.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Wooden & Low Crossbar
metas.note: Wooden poles with a lowered crossbar are mostly found in Sinaloa and Sonora.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Yellow Edge Road Divider
metas.note: This road divider with a yellow top and bottom edge is found all along the 95D from Mexico City to Acapulco.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Yellow Lamp Post
metas.note:
Most lamp posts and lamp arms in Aguascalientes city are yellow.

NOTE: They are not exclusive and are only very common.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Zig-Zag Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a zig-zag bent pole arm is found in Hermosillo.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Bamboo Snow Pole
metas.note: Bamboo snowpoles are regional and can mostly be found in Innlandet, Akershus, Østfold, Buskerud and Vestfold but can also be found rarely in Trøndelag, Vestland, Agder, Telemark and Rogaland.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Bergen Hydrant
metas.note: You can find this specific design of green fire hydrants in Bergen.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Big Wooden Snowpole
metas.note: Big wooden sticks are found on roads that are covered with snow almost the entire year. So far, they've been spotted on the road that runs north of Hardangervidda National Park, on the road west of Jotunheimen and southwest of Valdres Natur-og kulturpark.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Black Snow Poles
metas.note: Black plastic snowpoles are more regional and will mostly be found in Trøndelag, Møre og Romsdal and Vestland, but can also be found in Nordland and more rarely in Innlandet, Buskerud, Rogaland and Telemark

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Oslo Pole Plate
metas.note: Fairly large black or red pole plates can be found in Oslo.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Rusty Guardrail
metas.note: Rusty guardrails are almost exclusively found in coastal regions, and particularly on the southern half of the west coast.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Senja Snowpoles
metas.note: Green plastic snowpoles are found mostly around the island of Senja in Troms since the company selling these is also located there. The company also sells other colors less frequently. These can also less commonly be found all over Troms and Finnmark.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Small Blue Snowpole
metas.note: Small blue snowpoles can be found around Elverum.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Two Red Stripes
metas.note: Two red stripes going around lamp posts are commonly found in Stavanger.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Wide Black ID
metas.note: Small, wide black pole plates, with a single line of letters and digits, can be found in southeastern Norway.

metas.name: Peru - Infrastructure - Boulevard Street
metas.note: Most of the boulevard-type streets in Peru are in the city of Lima. These boulevards are typically long, straight streets divided by concrete or a grassy berm.

metas.name: Peru - Infrastructure - Cigarette Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, with a black and yellow stripe at the top, is unique to the state of Moquegua, which is located in the south of Peru.

metas.name: Peru - Infrastructure - Divided Highway
metas.note:
Highway 1N/S is divided in the highlighted area on the map.

NOTE: It is the only divided highway outside of cities.

metas.name: Peru - Infrastructure - Northern Tuk Tuks
metas.note:
Tuk-Tuks with open front compartments are primarily found in the northern half of Peru, and are especially common in northern Amazonian adjacent regions.

NOTE: This type of Tuk-Tuk can be found elsewhere to a lesser extent, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Peru - Infrastructure - Pucallpa
metas.note:
The east-central Amazonian city of Pucallpa, which lies close to the Brazil border, has a consistent street grid of WSW to ENE.

NOTE: Some northern and eastern areas of the city feature grids of different orientation.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Acne Blocks
metas.note: The southern peninsula of Quezon has these sloped concrete blocks with round spots made from small rocks that kind of look like a skin issue. Blocks in this style with straight edges are common throughout the country, and you can get slanted concrete blocks without the acne in other places as well, but the combination is exclusive to this area.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver, who is quoting sleepfor8hx3 on a document that unfortunately is not available at this point in time (2025/04/08)

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Bataan Death March
metas.note:
These large decorated white waystones, commemorating the Bataan Death March, can be seen along roads going from Mariveles and Bagac in the south to San Fernando in the north.

NOTE: The Bataan Death March continued from San Fernando to Capas by train, where a larger memorial has been built.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Bicol Stripes
metas.note: White guardrails with three recurring black stripes are unique to the region of Bicol in southern Luzon.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Black & Yellow Guardrail
metas.note: In the Cordillera Administrative Region you can find yellow and black striped concrete guardrails.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Double Pancake Insulator
metas.note: Double pancake insulators are very rare, but most likely to be found along the coast of East Samar, from about the height of the island of Hilabaan all the way down to the southern tip.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Indented Pole
metas.note: Square concrete poles with an indent on both side, similar to the poles found in Chile, are mainly found north of Manila and in and around the city of Bacolod on the island of Negros.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - K-Waystone
metas.note:
These waystones with K and a number below show the distance related to Manila (or the max distances on specific islands)

This number can be used to narrow down guesses.

For example, certain islands cannot exceed the orange numbers on the image. As another example, Mindanao, and nowhere else, always has numbers above 1000.
metas.footer: Source: philippines km=0 marker by bullfrogggy

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Ladder Poletop
metas.note:
A poletop made up of two tall vertical metal bars having an L-shaped cross-section which are connected via several thin wires, making it resemble a ladder, is unique to Manila and the surrounding area.

NOTE: You may sometimes come across similar looking poletops, with square bars instead of L-shaped ones, throughout the entire country. They will however almost never have more than two connecting wires.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Northern Cebu Yellow Blocks
metas.note: In northern Cebu, you will find gray concrete guard blocks with their edges painted yellow.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver, who is quoting sleepfor8hx3 on a document that unfortunately is not available at this point in time (2025/04/08)

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Northwest-Leyte & Biliran Insulator
metas.note: Three ridges plus a long extender at the top to carry the wire are most commonly found in Leyte and Biliran.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Palawan Highway
metas.note:
The highway going south from Puerto Princesa on Palawan can be characterised by being very wide, often featuring six lanes, while simultaneously having very little traffic.

Along the road you will usually see this double electrical wire, which can help confirm your guess.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Quad Insulator
metas.note: This cylinder with four distinct ridges is most common in Ilocos Norte, but can also be found in Biliran.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Quad Pancake Insulator
metas.note: If you see a quadruple pancake insulator on a pole top, you're going to be on the one road with coverage in Davao Occidental, along the coast, between approximately Don Marcelino and Bukid.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Sausage Insulator
metas.note: This grey insulator with lots of small ridges that looks kind of solid is most common in and around Manila, but can rarely be found elsewhere.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Siquijor Lamp
metas.note: Lamp posts on Siquijor are typically painted yellow, with black stripes at the bottom.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Square Metal Mesh Poles
metas.note:
Square metal mesh poles are found on Mindanao, mainly on the Zamboanga peninsula.

NOTE: Most of the poles found outside of the Zamboanga peninsula are found along highways and have poletops with three hanging insulators.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Star Wars Insulator
metas.note: This type of insulator that looks like the buildings on Tatooine is most common in northern Luzon and in and around Manila.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Dipolog City
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

Dipolog City likes to have the tiniest window imaginable over the driver’s side of the car & a big number on the roof.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Isulan
metas.note: These trikes with the large flat black roof, the small side window and no lines in the main window are found in Sultan Kudarat mainly. These green trikes with blue POBLACION text on them are specific to Isulan.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Ozamiz City
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

One city-specific variant to note is this one, with these bubbly numbers on top of the driver’s window (the trike itself can be any color scheme), which are exclusive to Ozamiz City and surrounding areas.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Square Roof
metas.note: These trikes with a square roof are also very common within Maguindanao.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Sultan Kudarat
metas.note: These trikes with the large flat black roof, the small side window and no lines in the main window are found in Sultan Kudarat mainly.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Tacurong City
metas.note: These trikes with the large flat black roof, the small side window and no lines in the main window are found in Sultan Kudarat mainly. This more colorful variant with a number on top is specific to Tacurong City.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Umbrella
metas.note:
These trikes with an umbrella are super common in Maguindanao, Misamis Occidental, and Lanao del Sur. Note that these are really the only trikes found in Cotabato city, so if there’s only these guys it’s a good clue for there.

NOTE: These are also very common in Cebu!
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga City
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

This trike is a Zamboanga city trike- they have a flat roof, a white line separating the passenger and the driver’s side. There’s a little bumper thing jutting out from under the window, and there’s still the vertical bit underneath the passenger’s window. Zamboanga city specifically has these super colorful trikes.

This type of trike is still identifiable from the back due to the black cloth roof, the large window with the singular white line, and the back having a side window. These less colorful variants can be found Northeast of the main city.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga City (non-colorful variant)
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

This trike is a Zamboanga city trike- they have a flat roof, a white line separating the passenger and the driver’s side. There’s a little bumper thing jutting out from under the window, and there’s still the vertical bit underneath the passenger’s window. Zamboanga city specifically has these super colorful trikes.

This type of trike is still identifiable from the back due to the black cloth roof, the large window with the singular white line, and the back having a side window. These less colorful variants can be found Northeast of the main city.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga Peninsula
metas.note:
This trike shape is essentially the only variant seen on the entire Zamboanga Peninsula. What sticks out to me is the passenger window shape- it’s kind of like an airplane window. Other notable parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window.

It’s identifiable from the back as well from the singular window in the back, as well as the roof tilting, and the random bars on top.

A common variant is this one with a large window hanging over the driver’s side. You can tell it’s the same type of trike from the same shape of the passenger car- where it has the airplane window (even if it’s horizontal) and then the bit beneath it that’s completely vertical and flat, along with the roof tilting back.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Yellow Backboards
metas.note: On the islands of Panay and Guimaras (the little island next to Iloilo), electricity counters are frequently mounted on yellow backboards. These can be horizontal or vertical, metal or wood.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver, who is quoting sleepfor8hx3 on a document that unfortunately is not available at this point in time (2025/04/08)

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - <-Pole
metas.note: Poles with 2 diagonal bars forming a ‘<’ shape can be found mostly in the northeastern provinces, most commonly in Limpopo and North West.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - A-Poletop (narrow)
metas.note: Poles with 3 bars forming the letter ‘A’, with the bottom insulators being attached at the edges of a horizontal bar, can be found almost exclusively in Western Cape, and rarely in bordering provinces.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - A-Poletop (wide)
metas.note: Poles with 3 bars forming the letter ‘A’, with the bottom insulators being attached directly to the 'A' rather than a horizontal bar, can be found in Eastern Cape.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Alternating Insulators
metas.note: Poles with 3 alternating insulators sticking out horizontally at the top are mostly seen in the four northern provinces of Limpopo, Gauteng, North West and Mpumalanga. They can also sometimes be found in Northern Cape. In the rest of the country, these pole tops are exceedingly rare.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Bird Nest
metas.note: Big bird nests on top of poles are commonly seen in the northern part of the Northern Cape Province.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Dodgy Adverts
metas.note: Poles or any public infrastructure will often be plastered with dodgy adverts for abortion services or penis enlargement pills in and around Gauteng, in particular in Johannesburg and Emalahleni.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Durban Lamp
metas.note: While this lamp and arm can be found uncommonly across the country, Durban uniquely has this bump on the top. You may, however, still see the standard lamp and arm.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Kruger National Park Waystone
metas.note: This distinctive directional waystone is commonly found at many junctions in Kruger National Park.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Limpopo Pavement
metas.note: You can find this grainy, almost Texas-like pavement with a hint of pink in Limpopo.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - M-Road - Durban
metas.note: Metropolitan Routes are major roads around cities. They are designated with the letter M. These distinct and unique M route signs are commonly found in Durban.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - M-Road - Gqeberha
metas.note: Metropolitan Routes are major roads around cities. They are designated with the letter M. These distinct and unique M route signs are commonly found in Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha)

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Metal Arms
metas.note: Poles with 1 or 2 metal arms holding up insulators are most commonly seen in Mpumalanga.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Powerplant
metas.note: Power plants are often seen in between the town of Secunda and eMalahleni in Mpumalanga.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Red Sticker
metas.note:
Square, red stickers on the back of regular signs are often found in Eastern cape and close to Eastern cape in Northern Cape and Free State. You may see them in the North West province as well, but to a lesser extent.

NOTE: Red stickers on the back of chevrons can be seen in almost every province.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Three Stripes
metas.note: Traffic lights and pedestrian crossing poles in Johannesburg are encircled by three strips of reflective tape.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Trident Pole
metas.note: Trident pole tops are almost unique to KwaZulu-Natal.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - White Sticker
metas.note: White stickers on the back of chevrons are often seen in the Cape provinces.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Bozcaada Tourist Sign
metas.note: These light blue and grey touristic signs which are either arrow shaped or rectangular with a half circle on the top can be found on the island of Bozcaada.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Chevron - Yellow on Black
metas.note: Yellow on black chevrons are mainly found in and around the Balıkesir Province in the west and in the Kars Province in the far east. Beware that you may very rarely find them elsewhere.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Chevron Black on Yellow
metas.note: Black on yellow chevrons are mainly found north of Izmir.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - European Poleplate
metas.note: In the European part of Turkey, except Istanbul, utility poles, and other electrical infrastructure, will have a 6 digit code, which is often seen on a small pole plate under the yellow electricity warning plate.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Highway without Divider
metas.note: Four-lane divided highways with no divider, other than double middle road lines, are almost exclusively found in the eastern half of the country.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Red Oval Sign
metas.note: Street signs in Trabzon and Yalvaç are red and oval-shaped. House numbers also feature the same design.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Streetsign - Ankara
metas.note:
Street signs in the Ankara Province are blue with a small round top. Similar street signs can very rarely be found in Giresun.

Beware that some newer street signs are red.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Streetsign - Bolu
metas.note: Street signs in Bolu are also green, but are completely flat and lack any kind of border.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Streetsign - Bursa
metas.note:
Street signs in Bursa are green, and generally have slightly extruded letters, meaning the signs are not completely flat.

NOTE: Several other types of infrastructure in Bursa, such as fences and guardrails, may also be coloured green.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Streetsign - Istanbul
metas.note:
Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in several cities. In the bottom right corner, you can find a white arrow and some numbers. If this arrow is pointing in both directions and has a single arrowhead, rather than double, then you are almost certainly in Istanbul.

Beware that simple arrows pointing in only one direction can be found in both Istanbul and in other cities. However, if you see such signs in combination with red house numbers, then you should be in Istanbul.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Streetsign - Izmir
metas.note: Street signs in the Izmir Province are dark blue, noticeably bulge outwards and very commonly have the emblem of Izmir in white at the top of the sign.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Watertank - Horizontal on top of Vertical
metas.note: Horizontal water tanks placed on top of vertical water tanks are primarily found in a line following the south coast and going up to Elâzığ.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Watertank - Octagonal
metas.note: Square water tanks with angled corners are found in the south, approximately from İskenderun to Sanliurfa.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Watertank - Spherical
metas.note: White spherical water tanks can be found in the southeast, mainly south of Batman.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Watertank - Vertical
metas.note: Vertical water tanks can be found in most of Turkey, but are notably uncommon along the south and west coast.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - 6 bolt bollard
metas.note:
This bollard has a white rectangular plate, with 6 bolts: 2 at the top, 2 in the middle and 2 at the bottom. There are different variants, with circular reflectors, rectangular reflectors, or no reflectors at all.

They're all found in California

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Adopt-A-Highway Signs
metas.note: Most states have unique, distinct and learnable Adopt-a-Highway signs, which can be seen on the side of roads. A map of those can be seen here. Keep in mind, some states have slight variations in design.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Arrow Street Number
metas.note:
North Carolina commonly uses a style of street signs showing street numbers and arrows in addition to the street name.

NOTE: Other states occasionally feature street signs with similar designs, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - ATV Route
metas.note: These green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Billboards
metas.note: Billboards are banned in Maine, Vermont, Alaska and Hawaii. So if you see one, you can rule those out.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Black Tar
metas.note: A black stripe can sometimes be seen in between the two yellow, middle road lines in California.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Black/White Overpass Support
metas.note: These stripes on an overpass support are a dead giveaway that it’s South Carolina. Sometimes a sign with yellow and black stripes is used instead
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - California Bridge Marker
metas.note: California posts these bridge markers (with a lot of numbers) on bridges. The county abbreviations used on the bridge markers are different from those on the postal markers.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - California Stripes
metas.note: Utility poles in California usually have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Chattanooga Font
metas.note: The city of Chattanooga in Tennessee has its own unique font that is used on some signs in the city.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Circular Fraction-Sign
metas.note: West Virginia sometimes features street signs with a symbol that resembles a fraction inside a circle.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Clearance on Overpass
metas.note: South Carolina is the only southeastern state to post the clearance on every overpass.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Concrete Pavement
metas.note:
Concrete paving on main highways is much more common in Iowa than in other states.

NOTE: Concrete paving on residential streets is commonly seen throughout the Midwest states and parts of the East Coast.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - County Road - Clark County
metas.note: Clark County is the county Las Vegas is situated in and it uses a unique county route shield.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Dark Wooden Fences
metas.note:
Dark-coloured wooden fences with several horizontal wooden supports are common in farming areas of central and southern Appalachia, stretching from Pennsylvania to Georgia.

NOTE: These types of fences can be found elsewhere to a lesser extent, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Diamond Bollard
metas.note:
The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.

NOTE: These bollards can be found to a lesser extent in other western states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Double Signposts
metas.note:
Signs attached to two signposts can be seen in Michigan. Not all signs are attached to two signposts.

NOTE: Double signposts can also be seen in other states, but are not as common.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - E-2 Sign
metas.note: In New Hampshire there will often be a white metal sign with the characters ‘E-2’ on it adjacent to the road, typically at either end of bridges.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Exit Ramp / No Parking
metas.note: Georgia likes to decorate its freeway offramps with no parking signs.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Exit with Speed Limit
metas.note: New Alabama coverage can have these combined exit/speed limit signs.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Florida Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is found in Florida.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green Overpass Marker
metas.note: Overpass bridges in Mississippi have green plaques with white numbers on them.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green US Route
metas.note: This green U.S. Route shield with the word business at the top is unique to Maryland.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green-White Sign
metas.note: This sign is Illinois-specific.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green/Red Bridge Marker
metas.note:
Maine, New Hampshire, and Massachusetts use small green and red rectangular signs to mark the ends of bridges and guardrails.

NOTE: Not all bridges and guardrails in these states will have these markers.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - H-Reflector
metas.note: Snowplowable raised pavement markers can only be found on highways in the eastern states shown in the image. They are built into the road and somewhat resemble the letter H.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Hanging Yellow Boxes
metas.note:
Many large intersections in Michigan have stop lights and signs that hang from wires that stretch across the middle of the intersection. These markers are commonly in yellow boxes.

NOTE: These are not completely unique to Michigan, but are most commonly seen there.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Highway Signs
metas.note: Maximum speed limits vary by state and territory. The maximum speed limits shown here will generally be seen on interstate highways. Some interstates and highways in their respective states or territories will have lower maximum speed limits than what is shown.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Horizontal Traffic Light
metas.note: Horizontal Traffic Lights are common in Nebraska, New Mexico, Texas and Louisiana. They also appear occasionally in Oklahoma, Louisiana and Georgia.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - ICE Warning
metas.note: Signs warning about ice (like this) are commonplace in Louisiana.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Indiana Blue Square

metas.note: These white reflectors on signposts are unique to Kansas. They are most commonly seen on ‘stop’ signs in rural areas.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Kentucky Rumble Strips
metas.note: Some roads and highways in the state of Kentucky use uniquely-shaped rumble strips that are thin, relatively long recessed lines on the very outside edges of the road.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Key West Poles
metas.note: Poles on Intersections in Key West have a white paint at the bottom which contains the name of the street its on.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Kilometer
metas.note:
Interstate 19 in Arizona from Tucson to the Mexico border uses kilometres on the exit and distance signs. This is the only part of the country that uses kilometres instead of miles for highway signs.

NOTE: Speed limit signs in this area still use MPH instead of KPH.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Large Center Line Gap
metas.note:
Yellow lines with a noticeably larger gap in between them are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oregon. They can also be found to a lesser extent in Washington, Alabama, and Michigan.

NOTE: Wide middle lines can also rarely appear in other states, so consider other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Letter Highway Sign (with County)
metas.note: Wisconsin and Missouri are the only two states that use a lettering system (A - ZZZ) for their county highways. Wisconsin signs typically have the word ‘county’ above the letter, while Missouri signs typically do not. The borders of the signs also vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Letter Highway Sign (without County)
metas.note: Wisconsin and Missouri are the only two states that use a lettering system (A - ZZZ) for their county highways. Wisconsin signs typically have the word ‘county’ above the letter, while Missouri signs typically do not. The borders of the signs also vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Lone Star
metas.note: Texas’s nickname is the Lone Star State. You can see the Texas star on the state’s flag. Many Texans use the star as a decoration on gates, for example.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Maine Roadlines
metas.note: Maine often uses a dashed single yellow line or a combination of dashed and solid instead of a solid double one in the middle of a road. I feel like Maine does it a bit more often than other states in the region.

metas.note: Some Interstate bridges in Maryland (but not the neighboring states or DC) seem to have this code painted on them. (Discovered by bagaboiebailey in the USA GeoGuessr Community server).

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Midwest Grainy Roads
metas.note: Some rural roads in the Upper Midwest use a similar road pavement to Texas. They will have a grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface, but will vary in colour. These roads are most common in the state of Illinois.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Mile Marker
metas.note: California doesn’t use mile markers.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Minnesota Bridge Sign
metas.note: In Minnesota, these yellow signs with vertical, black triangles are placed before bridges at most major river crossings and at the beginnings and ends of guardrail sections on large highways.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Minnesota Stop Sign
metas.note: On most rural ‘stop’ signposts in Minnesota, a black-and-white marker is attached to the posts horizontally. The shape may vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Nashville Bins
metas.note: Nashville has trash bins with the recognizable logo.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - National Parks
metas.note:
Guardrails, signs, and signposts are commonly painted a medium brown colour in US National Parks, which are often located in the west. Guardrails that are painted brown can be made out of both wood and metal. Rock walls can also sometimes be seen in place of guardrails.

NOTE: There are occasional exceptions to this rule, so consider other clues before guessing in a National Park.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Nevada Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Nevada Mile Marker
metas.note: Top part has the highway name. The middle part is an abbreviation of the county name. The lower part has the mile number.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - New Hampshire Interstate Sign
metas.note: These signs should only be found in NH (notice the dividing line between the two numbers).
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - New Hampshire US Route Sign
metas.note: These are also specific to New Hampshire. Notice the dividing line on the sign.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - New Jersey - 500 Series County Routes
metas.note: These county routes are given unique three-digit numbers that begin with a 5. There is only one route per number. The same number cannot be duplicated in multiple counties. There is therefore only one County Route 525 in the entire state of New Jersey. What’s also interesting about the 500 Series routes is that they follow the same cardinal direction rule as Interstates: even-numbered routes run east-to-west and odd-numbered ones north-to-south. In common with the U.S. Routes, the numbers increase southward.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - New Orleans Circle
metas.note: This circular windshield sticker is found in New Orleans, Louisiana.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - No Middle Line
metas.note:
Some small roads in California lack a middle yellow line; instead only feature solid white lines on each side of the road.

NOTE: This can rarely be seen in other states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - North Carolina - Circular Pay to Park
metas.note: Raleigh, NC uses circular pay to park signs to indicate parking meter locations. (unlike Charlotte, NC)

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - North Carolina / Blue Parking Sign
metas.note: Charlotte uses green parking signs, whereas Raleigh uses blue parking signs.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - North Carolina Signpost
metas.note: White signs attached to signposts can commonly be seen in North Carolina.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Number + Direction Road
metas.note:
Streets in Utah and Idaho, particularly in urban areas, are often named by using a combination of a number and cardinal direction (i.e. ‘600 South.’)

NOTE: This style of street naming can be found rarely in other Western states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Oak Streetsign
metas.note: Oakland has this tree on their street name signs.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Oil Pumpjack
metas.note: Oil pumpjacks are short, industrial-looking metal structures located at the surface of oil fields and are used to pump crude oil from the earth below. They are most common in western states, particularly in Texas, Eastern New Mexico, and North Dakota.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Oklahoma Stopsigns
metas.note: In Oklahoma, you can often find a green rectangular sign with 3 rows of numbers attached to the back of stop signs at rural intersections

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Overpass Milemarker
metas.note: In Alabama, overpasses have these mile markers hanging from them.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Parish
metas.note: Louisiana doesn’t call its counties counties but uses the word parish instead. This is a relic of the French colonial past of the state. You might occasionally spot the word on an intersection sign, for example. The location is guaranteed to be in Louisiana because no other state uses the word parish in that way.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Pennsylvania Intersection Signs
metas.note: Rectangular white signs can sometimes be seen attached to signposts at intersections in Pennsylvania. On top, the number of the converging state route is written.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Pillar Stripes
metas.note: Alabama likes to glue these stripes to overpass support pillars.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Pittsburgh Bridges
metas.note: Many bridges are used to connect the various neighbourhoods of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. These expansive, steel bridges are commonly painted bright yellow. Additionally, Pittsburgh is easy to identify because of it being flanked by 3 rivers and steep bluffs on all sides.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Pittsburgh Reflectors
metas.note: These circular reflectors are found in Pittsburgh.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Postal Marker
metas.note: Instead of Mile Markers, California uses postal markers that are white instead of green and have a county abbreviation.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Property Markers
metas.note:
A horizontal blue, red, or green sign can commonly be seen at the ends of driveways in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula. The house number is present, in addition to either the town name and or the road name (usually.)

NOTE: Nearby states often use similar markers, but typically lack any town or street name information and only feature numbers.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Rectangular Reflector
metas.note: These rectangular raised pavement markers are found in the south and west of the US and also in Massachusetts.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Red Streetsign
metas.note: Mesa, a city next to Phoenix, sometimes uses these red street name signs in the western part of the city.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Roadname on Sidewalk
metas.note:
In San Francisco, CA, almost every intersection has the road name written on the sidewalk.

This is due to the many earthquakes in this city, making sure every road is still labeled in case the streetsigns fall off.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Rock Walls
metas.note:
In rural areas of Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire, short rock walls are commonly visible adjacent to the road.

NOTE: These rock walls can be found rarely in adjacent states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Small Circle Bollard
metas.note: Roadside bollards in Wyoming often feature a dark metal pole with a white circular reflector at the top. The top of the metal pole is sometimes painted white or grey, which is unique to Wyoming.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Small Green Signs
metas.note:
Vermont features small rectangular green signs on stop sign posts with three rows of horizontal numbers. The top row of numbers correlates to the highway or road number that the road with the stop sign intersects with.

The State of New York uses similar style signs. However, these signs can be attached to different types of sign posts (town entry signs, highway signs, etc.)

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - South Carolina Intersection Signs
metas.note: Black street signs with white text can commonly be found at intersections in South Carolina.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - SPEED Sign
metas.note: Speed signs in Oregon often simply have the word ‘Speed’ instead of the standard ‘Speed Limit’.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Square Guardrail
metas.note:
Square guardrails are the most dominant (but not the only) type of guardrail in the states of New York and Wyoming. They have a long bar across the top, with several square legs supporting them.

NOTE: These guardrails can be found, to a lesser extent, in some adjacent states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Texas Bands
metas.note:
Yellow or red bands can commonly be seen around signposts in Texas.

NOTE: Similar reflectors can sometimes be seen in other states, such as Hawaii.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Texas Grainy Roads
metas.note:
Texan roads often have a grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface.

NOTE: Similar pavement can sometimes be seen in adjacent states such as New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Colorado.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Thick Black / Thinner Yellow Sign
metas.note: The black stripes on these signs are a bit thicker in Louisiana than in other states.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Thick Lines
metas.note:
Some roads in West Virginia, Virginia, and Maryland use middle yellow lines that are thicker than traditional yellow road lines.

NOTE: These are not present on all roads in these states, and can be found elsewhere, so use this tip in conjunction with other clues.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Trolley - Miami
metas.note: The Greater Miami area has a so-called trolley system which is a free public transport system. Different towns have different colors in their trolleys. The Miami Trolley is orange at the top and green at the bottom, with a small white stripe in between (the colors of the Miami-Dade flag, which are the same as the Indian flag).

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Trolley - Miami Beach
metas.note: The Greater Miami area has a so-called trolley system which is a free public transport system. Different towns have different colors in their trolleys. The Miami Beach Trolley is blue.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Vertical House Number
metas.note:
Properties in rural and exurban Ohio, Lower Michigan, and Indiana commonly feature a vertically-oriented metal sign with white numbers, indicating the house number of the adjacent building. These signs are most commonly blue or green, and are commonly attached to mailboxes.

NOTE: These may be rarely found in other states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Virginia Intersection Signs
metas.note: Rectangular white signs can sometimes be seen at intersections in Virginia.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Washington Bollard
metas.note: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Waymo
metas.note: Waymo is an autonomous driving company which offers taxi services in several cities. Its cars are very distinct, have a lidar on top and notably have no person sitting behind the wheel.
